jobs.title: Designer - Partnerships
jobs.excerpt: What are we building? Hard Rock Digital is a fiercely focused team working to become the best online sportsbook, casino, and social gaming company in the world.
jobs.description:
What are we building?

Hard Rock Digital is a fiercely focused team working to become the best online sportsbook, casino, and social gaming company in the world. We're building a deeply curious team with a passion for learning, operating, and building new products and technologies for millions of consumers. We're customer-obsessed — we care about each customer interaction, experience, behavior, and insight, and strive to ensure we're always acting authentically.

Rooted in the kindred spirits of Hard Rock and the Seminole Tribe of Florida, Hard Rock Digital taps a brand known the world over as the leader in gaming, entertainment, and hospitality. We're taking that foundation of success and bringing it to the digital space - ready to join us?

What’s the position?

As a Designer supporting Partnerships Creative, you’ll help shape how Hard Rock Bet connects with fans through our team and league partnerships (NFL, NBA, NHL, racing, and more). You’ll concept and design co-branded assets that elevate how our brand shows up across digital, social, in-venue, and experiential environments, driving both awareness and cultural relevance. From arena signage to social and digital campaigns, you’ll help fans experience the thrill of Hard Rock Bet wherever they watch or play.

You’ll collaborate closely with the Design Lead, creative team, and cross-functional partners to bring ideas to life and ensure every execution aligns with both internal brand standards and partner guidelines. Your primary mission will be to support the design and execution of partnerships creative primarily within the Sportsbook segment

What You’ll Do

  • Support the Creative Pod: Support the Awareness designers on larger campaign initiatives by extrapolating creative into additional sizes, versions, and placements

  • Asset Production: Create and adapt co-branded design assets for various partners and channels including social media, email, web, print, and experiential activations

  • Versioning & Resizing: Execute multiple versions of creative based on templates or master designs, ensuring accuracy and consistency.

  • File Prep & Delivery: Prepare final files for production, including packaging, exporting, and formatting for various platforms, partners, and vendors.

  • Quality Assurance: Review and proof assets for errors, ensuring pixel-perfect execution and adherence to both partner and internal brand guidelines.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with designers, project managers, and marketing teams to meet deadlines and deliverables.

  • Stay Ahead of Trends by keeping up-to-date with the latest design trends and best practices in digital and print advertising, particularly within the Sportsbook landscape.

Our ideal candidate

You’re a designer who thrives at the intersection of sports, culture, and creativity - a problem-solver who understands that great design is both strategic and emotional, connecting fans to brands through visual storytelling. You are more than just a designer; you are a problem-solver who understands that a great design must also be effective. You are detail-oriented, hungry to learn, and thrive on seeing your work make a real-time impact. You enjoy the challenge of a fast-paced environment and are excited by the idea of designing to see your work come to life across arenas, social feeds, and the biggest sports moments of the year.

Requirements

We’re looking for:

  • 3+ years of experience in production design or graphic design.

  • A strong portfolio demonstrating co-branded campaigns and/or multi-format execution (print, digital, experiential), versioning and resizing, and template-based work.

  • Mastery of the Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign) is essential. Experience with Figma is a major plus.

  • Detail-oriented with excellent organizational and time management skills.

  • Well-versed in designing for print (both large and small formats) and digital platforms.

  • Experience working in fast-paced, deadline-driven environments.

  • Familiarity with asset management systems and file organization best practices.

  • Collaborative mindset: Experience working with marketers and product teams to refine creative approaches.

  • A passion for or interest in sports or the iGaming industry is a significant advantage.

The treasures you shall reap

We offer our employees more than just competitive compensation and benefits. Our team benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Flexible vacation allowance. 

  • Remote or Hybrid Flexibility: Enjoy the flexibility of remote work, with opportunities for in-person collaboration at our Austin headquarters at least twice a year, or a hybrid arrangement.

  • Innovative Environment: Join a team that thrives on pushing boundaries.

  • Growth Opportunities: As we scale, your role will evolve, providing you with unlimited opportunities for personal and professional growth.

  • Diverse and Inclusive: Join a team that values diversity, inclusivity, and embraces varied perspectives.

  • Backing of a globally recognized brand and enterprise-level resources

Roster of uniques 

We care deeply about every interaction our customers have with us, and trust and empower our staff to own and drive their experience. Our vision for our business and customers is built on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where, regardless of background or beliefs, you feel able to be authentic and bring all your talent into play. We want to celebrate you being you (we are an equal opportunity employer).

jobs.title: LIMS Data Specialist (OPEN - Anywhere in Canada, Ontario, CA)
jobs.excerpt: Basic Purpose: The Specialist is responsible for collaborating with the team to drive and optimize Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) projects.
jobs.description:
Basic Purpose:

The Specialist is responsible for collaborating with the team to drive and optimize Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) projects. The role will also have accountabilities and responsibilities related to various components/attributes of LIMS (ex. Test codes, EDDs, etc.) while also developing comprehensive data visualization solutions to enhance operational efficiency, customer service, and strategic decision-making across the organization.

The role involves close collaboration with Customer Service, Operations, management, programmers, and Business Analysts. Facilitating effective communication and project development is fundamental.

Key Accountability/Responsibilities:

  • The Specialist will review and write LIMS Proposal Requests, ensuring comprehensive documentation and capturing all necessary information. They will draft detailed Project Change Documents (PCDs) and submit them to Business Analysts for review, while simultaneously developing Tableau dashboards that provide actionable insights across departments.
  • The role involves close collaboration with programmers and Business Analysts, facilitating effective communication and project development. The Specialist will test implemented LIMS changes to ensure accuracy and functionality, and create interactive reports using Tableau that translate complex data into understandable visualizations.
  • Additionally, they will implement EDD (Electronic Delivery) Builder protocols to standardize report generation and automate data transfer mechanisms. The Specialist will work closely with staff to identify existing LIMS solutions, promote efficiency, and provide strategic assessments to leadership regarding project viability and implementation efforts.
  • Continuous improvement is a key focus, with the Specialist driving efficiency within LIMS and related systems while ensuring adherence to regulatory conditions for external and internal clients. They will support development and maintenance of Tableau dashboards that integrate multiple data sources, optimize performance, and provide comprehensive documentation of visualization processes. They will develop and maintain Power BI dashboards where Tableau dashboards are not available.
  • The Specialist will have experience with SQL database management systems and will be required to generate data pulls to support individual operational continuous improvement initiatives.
  • The role requires participation in department and Health & Safety meetings, maintenance of training records, and compliance with Bureau Veritas Code of Ethics Policy and quality systems.
  • All other responsibilities as assigned.

Skills and Knowledge:

  • Post-secondary education in science, computer science or data science
  • 5+ years of experience in laboratory information systems, preferably with MaxxLIMS
  • Proficiency with Tableau Desktop, Tableau Server/Online, and Tableau Prep Builder is an asset
  • Strong understanding of data visualization principles and best practices
  • Proficiency with PowerBi is an asset
  • Experience in SQL and data manipulation
  • Ability to work with large and complex datasets
  • Proficiency in LIMS software and related technologies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
  • Ability to translate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience in project management and process improvement
  • Familiarity with laboratory operations and workflows
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work in a team environment
  • Adaptability and willingness to learn new technologies and processes
  • Ability to effectively collaborate with diverse stakeholders across different locations

Working Conditions:

  • Mainly in an office environment or remote work setup.
  • Extended periods of computer use for dashboard development and data analysis.
  • May require occasional flexible working hours to accommodate national team meetings.
  • Mental effort required for problem-solving, data analysis, and creative dashboard design.
  • High level of visual attention required for data visualization and quality assurance.

Additional Benefits Include:

Paid Time Off, Statutory Holidays, and up to 8 hours of volunteer time off

Life Insurance & AD&D

STD & LTD Coverage

Company RRSP match

Employee Assistant Program (EAP)

Professional Development through Tuition Reimbursement

Bureau Veritas is proud to be committed to providing fair and competitive pay.

The annual salary range for this role is $60 - 75k (depending on experience/quallifications)

jobs.description:
Located in the metropolitan area of Sacramento, the Adventist Health corporate headquarters have been based in Roseville, California, for more than 40 years. In 2019, we unveiled our WELL-certified campus - a rejuvenating place for associates systemwide to collaborate, innovate and connect.

Whether virtual or on campus, Adventist Health Roseville and shared service teams have access to enjoy a welcoming space designed to promote well-being and inspire your best work.

Job Summary:

Codes for cancer center encounters and maintains required quality and productivity standards while remaining compliant with third party, state and federal regulations. Reviews and resolves medical necessity edits that may apply for any outpatient surgical encounters, applying hospital and professional modifiers to CPT codes and processes any errors associated with the revenue cycle process. Assists in the design and implementation of workflow changes to reduce coding and billing errors. Uses knowledge of data collection systems for medical records. Reviews medical record documentation and accurately assigns appropriate ICD-10-CM diagnoses, CPT codes and modifiers as applicable for both the hospital and professional claim. Validates and processes any medical necessity edits (local or national coverage determinations) that may apply for hospital and professional coding. Monitors Discharged Not Billed (DNB) accounts, and as a team, ensure timely, compliant processing of outpatient and inpatient encounters through the hospital and professional revenue cycle. Codes and posts charges for outpatient complex cancer center procedures and diagnoses for the purpose of reimbursement, research, statistical data gathering, and compliance. Queries physicians when code assignments are not straightforward or documentation in the record is inadequate, ambiguous, or unclear for coding purposes. Maintains current knowledge of coding guidelines and reimbursement reporting requirements. Demonstrates a high degree of independence in performance of responsibilities, working effectively without direct supervision.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required
  • Experience with RadOnc and MedOnc coding: Required
  • Experience in an acute care setting: Preferred
  • Experience with Varian, Aria, Mosaiq and Cerner Oncology programs: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Radiation Oncology Certified Coder (ROCC) certification: Required

Essential Functions:

  • Develops physician and departmental relationships. Creates physician and coder education for cancer center specialty.

Working at Thoropass

At Thoropass, we are revolutionizing the compliance and audit industry by integrating cutting-edge AI technology with expert human insight. Our team is dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experiences and high-quality outcomes.

We’re driven by our mission to build a world that’s safer for consumers and ensuring compliance is never a blocker to innovation. By bringing together remarkably talented individuals, we’re looking to help the industry see compliance as an advantage. Join us as we collaborate to establish our platform as the world's leading choice for compliance and audit solutions.

Our Values

These are the behaviors and skills we look for in our people. Living by these values ensures we are building a team that can grow together and deliver the best possible outcomes for each other and our customers.

  • Take thoughtful risk: We solve for today while being considerate of tomorrow—creatively leveraging our tools and abilities to hit ambitious goals.
  • Be curious, ask, and learn: We always seek to better understand our industry and our customers. We don’t shy away from mistakes—using every bit of data to learn and iterate.
  • Win together: Compliance is a team sport. We proactively engage with one another and check our egos at the door in search of the best ideas.
  • Move the needle: Our goals are lofty for a reason. We set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and challenge ourselves to close the gap between those goals and results.

What We Do

Thoropass is transforming the landscape of security compliance and audits. As the only all-in-one platform that combines compliance automation software with a tech-enabled audit firm and pentest services, we offer a modern approach to information security compliance and audit. Our AI-powered solutions, such as First Pass AI, are designed to streamline compliance and accelerate audits for frameworks like SOC, PCI, ISO, HITRUST, HIPAA, and more. Thousands of companies trust Thoropass for high-quality audit and assessment services, delighting in a truly differentiated experience.

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Thoropass has rapidly expanded with $97M in funding from top investors including J.P. Morgan, PayPal Ventures, Fin Capital, Centana, Canapi, and Bain Capital. We operate as a virtual, global company with a presence in over 18 countries. With substantial growth in both customers and revenue, we are strategically positioned for continued expansion in 2025 and beyond.

About the Role

Forget everything you think you know about information security auditing. We’re on a mission to reinvent the outdated, clunky audit process—and we’re doing it with cutting-edge AI, automation, and a relentless commitment to customer success.

At Thoropass, auditing isn’t about manually sifting through endless evidence or checking boxes—it’s about solving complex security problems for our customers in smarter, faster, and more innovative ways. And thanks to our AI-powered auditor tech stack and industry leading audit process, you won’t spend your days buried in audit testing.

If you’re an experienced, customer-centric auditor who’s tired of the grind and ready to help disrupt the industry, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Do

You’ll be the driving force behind a seamless ISO audit experience for our customers. With the help of your team and our powerful tech, you’ll transform audits from a chore into a strategic advantage.

Here’s what your day will look like:

  • Lead with Confidence: You’ll serve as the trusted advisor and main point of contact for your assigned customers, owning the ISO audit lifecycle from start to finish.
  • Review, Guide, Elevate: Analyze audit evidence requests submitted by customers, provide expert feedback, and guide them toward best practices.
  • Collaborate with AI: Partner with our advanced AI engine and auditor team to validate evidence, streamlining the process for maximum efficiency.
  • Deliver Excellence: Generate high-quality ISO audit reports that reflect accuracy, precision, and your professional expertise.
  • Problem-Solve Creatively: Use your curiosity and analytical skills to solve unique challenges, ensuring every customer has an exceptional experience.

What You’ll Bring

We’re looking for innovators, problem solvers, and tech enthusiasts with the following experience and skills:

  • ISO Expertise: At least 3+ years of ISO 27001 audit experience, including leading audit interviews.
  • Cloud Savvy: Familiarity with advanced cloud technologies (AWS, GCP, Azure).
  • Customer-First Attitude: Comfort working directly with customers and a knack for building relationships.
  • Technical Credentials: Currently possess or are pursuing certifications like ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, CISSP, CISA, CSP specific certifications like AWS Solutions Architect, or similar.
  • Sharp Mindset: Exceptional problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and analytical ability.
  • Curiosity & Drive: A genuine interest in solving problems and questioning the status quo.

Why You’ll Love This Role

  • No Manual Testing: Say goodbye to the drudgery of manual audit testing—our automation and dedicated audit experts do the heavy lifting.
  • Cutting-Edge Tech: Work with an AI-powered toolset designed to make your job easier and more impactful.
  • Make an Impact: Join a team that’s redefining how audits are done, creating value for customers in an entirely new way.

LATAM Compensation:

  • Exceptional private healthcare
  • Early equity in a fast-growing company
  • Work-from-home model
  • Flexible PTO
  • Company-provided laptop
  • Monthly wellness and home Wi-Fi stipend

Equal Opportunity

Within the Hybrid AI Multi-Environment Runtime, this role owns how AI services and agents are built and deployed, how models execute, how requests are routed to them, how AI assets are catalogued and governed, how consumption is measured and bounded, and how the entire platform is observed across cloud, on-prem, edge, and air-gapped environments.

This role owns the delivery and runtime surface, including the CI/CD/CV pipelines that ship AI workloads, secure model execution, semantic routing, and model/prompt selection, together with the governance, discovery, cost, and telemetry systems that keep AI workloads shippable, economical, discoverable, and transparent.

This role is ideal for an engineer who is equally comfortable building automated delivery pipelines, operating high-performance inference (GPUs, model servers, sandboxed execution), and building deep observability and cost visibility; who understands that in regulated contexts every AI workload must be delivered repeatedly and every AI request must be economically bounded, attributable, and traceable end-to-end.

Responsibilities:

  • Own DevOps and delivery for AI workloads: build and operate the CI/CD/CV pipelines that ship AI services, agents, and runtime components, including automated build, test, continuous verification, release, and rollback, so AI workloads are delivered repeatedly and safely into every environment.
  • Own governance and discovery for AI assets, including service catalog/registry (Artifactory/Nexus, Harbor), experiment tracking and model metadata (MLflow), upstream registries/mirrors (HuggingFace/NGC), CVE/SBOM scanning (Trivy), lineage contracts (OpenLineage), and license management.
  • Own resource and cost management, including quotas and rate limits, cost attribution and utilization (Apptio/OpenCost/Kubecost), so AI execution stays economically bounded and controllable per tenant and engagement.
  • Own the full observability stack, including metrics (Prometheus/Mimir), logs (Loki), traces (Tempo/Jaeger), dashboards (Grafana), LLM debugging and evaluation (LangSmith/Langfuse), and SLA/alert notifications.
  • Own the OpenTelemetry collection layer, including multi-tenant receiver, exporters and queues (Kafka sink), DCGM exporter for GPU telemetry, processor batching, and dynamic filtering, so every signal is captured and routed reliably.
  • Automate GitOps-based delivery and continuous verification; embedding quality, integrity, and cost gates into pipelines so releases are policy-compliant by default rather than by manual review.
  • Close the loop between delivery and observability by using telemetry, evaluation, and cost signals to drive deployment decisions, progressive rollout, and automated rollback of AI workloads.
  • Ensure cost and telemetry are identity-stamped and per-tenant, so consumption and behavior are attributable end-to-end, keeping FinOps and observability tied to the workloads that generate the load.

Requirements:

  • Strong DevOps expertise: CI/CD/CV pipeline design, GitOps, continuous verification, and progressive/automated release and rollback for production workloads.
  • Deep expertise operating model-serving and inference systems (Ray, vLLM/Triton/NIM) on GPUs at production scale.
  • Deep observability skills: metrics, logs, traces, and OpenTelemetry.
  • FinOps mindset: able to attribute, bound, and optimize AI consumption cost per tenant and workload.
  • Familiarity with model/artifact governance, registries, CVE scanning, and license/lineage tracking.
  • Comfortable operating across cloud, on-prem, edge, and air-gapped environments with consistent runtime and telemetry semantics.
  • Strong communicator able to explain runtime, cost, and observability tradeoffs to engineers, architects, and leadership.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or related technical field.
  • 8+ years in DevOps, MLOps, platform, or observability engineering, with hands-on production ownership of AI or high-throughput services.
  • Strong hands-on DevOps experience, including CI/CD/CV pipelines and GitOps tooling (ArgoCD, Helm, GitHub Actions/GitLab CI, or equivalents) for automated build, test, release, and rollback.
  • Hands-on expertise operating inference/model-serving frameworks (Ray Serve, vLLM, Triton, or NIM) on GPU infrastructure.
  • Strong experience with observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo/Jaeger) and OpenTelemetry.
  • Experience with API gateways and request routing (Envoy or equivalent), including streaming responses.
  • Experience with cost management / FinOps tooling (OpenCost, Kubecost, or equivalent) and quota/rate-limit enforcement.
  • Familiarity with model/artifact registries and supply-chain scanning (Harbor, MLflow, Trivy/SBOM).
  • Proven track record operating AI or service infrastructure under compliance, security, or regulatory constraints.
  • Ability to define clean ownership boundaries and consumption contracts with platform, trust, and data teams.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with LLM evaluation and debugging tooling (LangSmith, Langfuse) and prompt/response quality measurement.
  • Experience with sandboxed/secure execution (gVisor, Firecracker, or microVM isolation) for untrusted or multi-tenant workloads.
  • Familiarity with GPU telemetry (DCGM) and GPU utilization optimization.
  • Experience with lineage and governance contracts (OpenLineage) and AI license management.
  • Exposure to multi-tenant cost attribution and per-tenant SLA/alerting.
  • Exposure to regulated delivery environments (financial services, tax, healthcare, risk).

jobs.excerpt: About UsSince 1989, SHI International Corp.  has helped organizations change the world through technology.
jobs.description:
About Us

Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services.

Over 17,000 organizations worldwide rely on SHI’s concierge approach to help them solve what’s next. But the heartbeat of SHI is our employees – all 7,000 of them. If you join our team, you’ll enjoy:

  • Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S.

  • Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities.

  • Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family.

  • World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours.

Job Summary

The Presales Solutions Architect – Enterprise Networking at SHI International is responsible for being SHI's Subject Matter Expert across the enterprise networking domain. The foundation of this role is core networking – routing and switching, campus LAN architecture, and WAN and SD-WAN design – with working breadth across enterprise wireless, network access control and segmentation, network management and observability, and network automation.

We are looking for depth in core networking first. Candidates who bring strong routing, switching, and WAN architecture experience and can speak credibly to the adjacent domains are encouraged to apply, even if their hands-on depth is uneven across every area listed below.

In this role, you will split your time between presales client engagements and internal practice development. On the presales side, you'll take a consultative approach, leading technical discovery sessions with clients to assess their network infrastructure maturity, designing target-state enterprise network architectures, and delivering compelling demos, POCs, and technical presentations. On the internal side, you'll build reusable collateral such as reference architectures, battle cards, and enablement content; evaluate and qualify new vendor partnerships; and conduct training sessions that keep our engineering and sales teams current on emerging network technologies, platform capabilities, and best practices.

Your credibility and technical depth will make you a trusted advisor to both SHI's most strategic customers and our internal stakeholders, driving meaningful network outcomes and revenue growth across the Networking practice.

This position is a remote position with Home Office setup as determined by SHI management.

Role Description

  • Design and deliver product demonstrations, proof-of-concepts (POCs), and technical presentations focused on enterprise networking solutions including campus routing and switching, enterprise wireless, SD-WAN and WAN edge, and network management and automation platforms
  • Lead technical discovery sessions to assess clients' network infrastructure maturity across campus, branch, wireless, WAN, and network operations capabilities
  • Translate complex networking concepts – such as dynamic routing design, Layer 2/Layer 3 segmentation, RF design and spectrum planning, application-aware routing, and QoS policy – into business-relevant value propositions for both technical and executive audiences
  • Design and present target-state enterprise network architectures covering campus LAN, wireless, branch and WAN/SD-WAN, high availability, network access control and segmentation, and integration with broader infrastructure stacks (security, cloud, data center, collaboration)
  • Support wireless engagements by leading discovery, interpreting predictive and validation survey output, framing high-density and IoT design considerations, and engaging specialist resources where deep RF design is required
  • Develop and maintain internal practice collateral including reference architectures, battle cards, competitive analyses, technical briefs, and vendor evaluation frameworks
  • Evaluate and qualify new vendor technologies and product capabilities; make recommendations on partner adoption, platform consolidation, and legacy solution retirement
  • Conduct internal enablement sessions for engineering and sales teams on emerging network technologies, product updates, use cases, and enterprise networking best practices
  • Drive revenue growth within the presales team by identifying new networking opportunities and optimizing service offerings
  • Collaborate with SHI stakeholder partner teams to create synergistic networking service solutions that integrate across SHI's broader portfolio
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key clients and partners, ensuring high levels of satisfaction and retention through product briefings, demonstrations, and knowledge transfer
  • Stay current with new networking technologies, protocols, and industry developments; track evolving architectures such as intent-based networking, cloud-managed networking, network-as-a-service, and private cellular to inform architectural recommendations
  • Contribute to practice development by identifying areas for growth, leading innovation initiatives, and creating and maintaining practice standards to ensure high-quality service delivery


Behaviors and Competencies


  • Adaptability: Can proactively adapt to challenging situations, anticipate changes, and make modifications to meet the demands of changing circumstances.
  • Communication: Can effectively communicate complex ideas and information to diverse audiences and can facilitate effective communication between others.
  • Documentation: Independently produces and maintains documentation for routine processes; ensures accuracy and consistency.
  • Leadership: Can proactively seek out leadership roles, initiate team projects, and contribute to team development and success.
  • Problem Solving: Can proactively identify potential problems, initiate preventive measures, and propose and contribute to innovative solutions.
  • Teamwork: Can lead a team effectively, facilitate cooperation, sharing information, and ensuring that all team members are able to contribute to their full potential.
  • Self – Motivation: Can proactively seek out challenges, initiate self-development projects, and contribute to personal or professional innovative ideas.

Skill Level Requirements


  • Strong proficiency in cloud architecture (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud).
  • Solid understanding of microservices, APIs, and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Expertise in solution design across enterprise systems, integration platforms, and data layers.
  • Strong background in system security, data privacy, and compliance.
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, business-oriented language.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automation tools, and infrastructure-as-code frameworks.
  • Proficient in software development methodologies (Agile, DevOps).
  • Excellent problem-solving, collaboration, and communication skills.

Other Requirements


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Network Engineering, Information Technology, or equivalent work experience
  • Minimum 6 years of experience in network engineering, enterprise network architecture, or infrastructure engineering roles, including hands-on routing, switching, and campus or WAN design and implementation
  • Demonstrated experience in presales, solutions architecture, or technical consulting within the networking or infrastructure domain
  • Experience presenting to customers, internal teams, or industry professional groups on networking topics
  • Exposure to at least two of the following adjacent areas: enterprise wireless, SD-WAN, network access control and segmentation, or network automation

The estimated annual pay range for this position is $180,000 - $250,000 which includes a base salary and bonus. The compensation for this position is dependent on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location and, therefore, will vary from individual to individual. Benefits may include, but are not limited to, medical, vision, dental, 401K, and flexible spending.

Equal Employment Opportunity – M/F/Disability/Protected Veteran Status

We are seeking an experienced OpenShift Platform Engineer to design, deploy, and operate enterprise-grade Red Hat OpenShift container platforms running mission-critical workloads across on-premises and cloud environments. In this role you will own the end-to-end platform lifecycle — from cluster provisioning and hardening, through workload onboarding and developer enablement, to ongoing operations and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in OpenShift and Kubernetes internals, strong Linux fundamentals, and a security-first mindset, and will partner with application teams, security engineers, and infrastructure stakeholders to deliver a stable, secure, and developer-friendly container platform.
Key Responsibilities
  • Architect, provision, and operate Red Hat OpenShift clusters across on-premises, virtualized, and major cloud environments, applying best practices for high availability, scalability, and security.

  • Onboard application development teams to the platform, providing clear self-service patterns, project templates, CI/CD integrations, and supporting documentation.
  • Operate OpenShift networking, including SDN/OVN-Kubernetes, ingress controllers, routes, network policies, and integration with enterprise firewalls and load balancers.
  • Manage OpenShift storage strategies (block, file, object), including dynamic provisioning, OpenShift Data Foundation, and integration with external storage platforms.
  • Implement comprehensive monitoring, logging, and tracing using the OpenShift observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, EFK, Tempo) and integrate with enterprise SIEM and APM tools.
  • Harden the platform in collaboration with security teams, including image scanning (Quay/Clair), runtime protection, secret management, and continuous compliance with regulatory frameworks.
  • Design and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines on OpenShift using Tekton, Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Argo Workflows, enabling safe and frequent application deployments.
  • Develop disaster-recovery and backup strategies for cluster state, etcd, and persistent workloads, validated through regular failover and restore drills.

  • Partner with application teams to right-size workloads, manage resource quotas, and tune cluster autoscaling for predictable performance and cost efficiency.
  • Continuously evolve platform tooling and developer experience, capturing feedback from internal users and translating it into roadmap improvements.
  • Mentor junior engineers and act as an OpenShift subject-matter expert across the broader organization.
Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Eight or more years of experience operating container platforms in production, with at least three years on Red Hat OpenShift.
  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of Kubernetes and OpenShift internals, including operators, CRDs, RBAC, and networking.
  • Strong Linux administration skills, including networking, performance tuning, and troubleshooting.
  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Ansible, Terraform, or Helm.
  • Solid experience implementing CI/CD pipelines on OpenShift or Kubernetes using Tekton, Jenkins, or Argo CD.
  • Strong scripting skills in Bash, Python, or Go.
  • Working knowledge of cluster monitoring, logging, and tracing tools.
  • Familiarity with container image security and supply chain hardening.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.description:
DeterTech's purpose is giving greater peace of mind to people and communities, every day – and that starts with trusting that the systems behind our products work as they should. This role provides dedicated, structured testing across Salesforce, integrations and other IT systems, so that changes are released with confidence rather than relying on technical staff to test their own work.
As the team's delivery capacity grows, this role removes the need for developers and administrators to coordinate and execute all testing themselves, freeing them to focus on building and supporting the platform. You will act as the quality champion across our core business systems—verifying changes across Salesforce Service Cloud, Field Service, MuleSoft APIs, business systems finance, manufacturing, and data connections with our Alarm Receiving Centre platform before features reach our teams and customers.

ABOUT DETERTECH
DeterTech is a security technology company operating across six countries, with principal UK sites in Prestwick and Telford. We predict, deter and detect risk on behalf of the people and communities we serve. Our values – Committed, Inclusive and Ambitious – shape how we work every day: we are accountable and deliver excellence; we collaborate and build trust; and we never stop learning while winning in the right way.

This is a remote role, with the flexibility to work from home. We also value face-to-face collaboration and would ask for some flexibility to attend occasional in-person meetings or team sessions.

Key Responsibilities

1. Test planning and design
• Develop test plans, test cases/scripts and test evidence for Salesforce, integration and wider IT system changes.
• Translate requirements and acceptance criteria into clear, well-structured test scenarios.
• Work closely with the Salesforce Lead, Solution Analyst, and Technical Delivery Manager during sprint planning to review user stories and build test scenarios before development begins.
• Create clear, repeatable test cases covering end-to-end operational journeys (such as lead-to-cash, engineer work order dispatch, and invoice creation across integrated systems).
2. Test execution
• Carry out system, integration and regression testing across Salesforce and other integrated business systems – not just websites or front-end applications.
• Execute manual test scripts and, where relevant, support automated testing.
• Test integration data flows and API triggers between MuleSoft, Salesforce, Finance and other business systems and the ARC software platform to ensure data passes accurately without loss or sync errors.
• Validate releases inside dedicated sandboxes and staging environments, partnering with administrators and developers using our release management tools (such as Copado) to ensure safe deployments.
• Help coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with departmental super-users and operational teams, ensuring feedback is captured clearly.
3. Defect management
• Identify, document, triage and retest defects, working closely with developers and administrators.
• Maintain clear, accurate defect and test records that the wider team can rely on.
• Log clear, reproducible bug reports with complete test steps, expected vs. actual results, and screenshots or system logs.
• Participate in defect triage meetings with the Technical Delivery Manager to prioritise fixes and prevent release delays.
4. Continuous improvement
• Help build a culture of quality across the team, recommending practical improvements to testing practices and coverage over time.
• Build and maintain a core regression test pack to protect critical business processes during regular sprint deployments and tri-annual Salesforce seasonal upgrades.
• Explore practical opportunities to introduce lightweight test automation for repetitive integration checks and core user journeys.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

Essential
• Demonstrable professional software/system testing experience.
• Experience with test planning, test cases/scripts and test evidence.
• System, integration and regression testing experience.
• Defect identification, documentation, triage and retesting experience.
• Ability to translate requirements/acceptance criteria into test scenarios.
• Experience testing integrated business systems, not just websites or front-end applications.
• Hands-on experience testing end-to-end business workflows across interconnected platforms (for example CRM, ERP, finance, or middleware APIs).
• Clear, practical communication skills, comfortable discussing bug steps and edge cases directly with developers, administrators, and non-technical stakeholders.
Desirable
• Experience testing Salesforce specifically (such as Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Field Service, or custom Flows) .
• Familiarity with test automation tools.
• ISTQB or an equivalent testing qualification.
• Experience working in an Agile delivery team using modern tools (such as Jira, Linear, or Azure DevOps).

jobs.excerpt: What We’re BuildingHoneycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do!
jobs.description:
What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!
If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb.io press releases.

Who We Are

We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.

How We Work

We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

Little more about the team:

AI is changing how software gets built, shipped, and run. It is increasing the need for sense-making of production software systems. We believe AI will reshape observability itself. Honeycomb created this category, and we want our next engineering leader to help us lead its reinvention.

The role

You’ll join the executive team as a full partner in setting strategy. Our exec team acts as a first team, working closely together to revise our strategy as the world changes. Right now, it is changing often! You’ll bring a wealth of experience and an imagination of what’s possible, help sharpen our bets, and decide with your peers the most elegant way forward. Then you’ll shape a strong engineering org to deliver on these decisions.

What you’ll do

  • Shape the strategy. Form your own view of where the product, technology and market are heading. Bring it to your closest partners: product and the CEO, and to the wider exec team. Some of our bets will need sharpening, and some new ones will need making.
  • Build alignment at the top. We believe our strength as a company depends on the strength of our exec team. We want you to make our exec team better, and for your first team to be the exec team. You’ll work closely with product and the CEO, challenging and being challenged in return, until the team is truly committed to a shared direction.
  • Help the whole org to make sense of fast change. When the ground moves quickly, people need help understanding what is changing and why. Burnout is high in our industry, and we want to keep our people motivated, excited to come to work, and with their full creativity and energy. You’ll explain engineering’s direction clearly and repeatedly, to engineers, managers, the exec team, and the rest of the company. We’re remote-first, so much of this happens in writing and in presentations.
  • Lead a high-performing team into what’s next. We have strong managers, directors, and ICs. You’ll aim that talent at our biggest opportunities and adjust the org’s structure, goals, and ways of working to be continually more effective. You’ll do this without losing what makes the team great.
  • Lead from technical credibility. You can’t lead an AI era shift without a deep understanding of the ergonomics of the landslide of change underway.

You might be a fit if

  • You’ve led engineering through large scale changes in direction, not just growth.
  • You’ve shipped software with AI tools yourself within the last 12 months.
  • You have a special talent for collaboration and improving executive teams.
  • You’re as interested in shaping strategy as in executing it.
  • You’ve worked at a larger company, and know what breaks as companies scale. But have a risk tolerance of someone from an early stage startup.
  • You’re comfortable with uncertainty, rapid change, and shaping new bets towards product-market fit.
  • You’ve led distributed teams and communicate well in writing and in person.
  • You care about developer tools and have good taste in them. (Having used Honeycomb is a bonus, not a requirement)
  • You share our values.

Worth reading: How we do business at Honeycomb in the AI era, our AI norms and values, and why engineering is all in on AI.

If you match some of this but not all of it, please apply anyway. We’d rather talk to a strong candidate who doubts themselves than miss them.

What you'll get when you join the Hive:

  • A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program
  • It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience
  • Time to recharge with unlimited PTO
  • A distributed-first mindset and culture (really!)
  • Home office, co-working, and internet stipend
  • Full benefits coverage for employees, with additional coverage available for dependents
  • Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, regardless of path to parenthood
  • Annual development allowance
  • And much more...
Please note we cannot currently sponsor or support visa transfers at this time. Additionally, in compliance with applicable law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work.

Phishing and Recruitment Scam Warning:

We take your security seriously. Please be aware that recruitment scams are increasingly common and scammers may create email addresses or websites to impersonate Honeycomb employees. To help protect you:
  • All communications will come from an @honeycomb.io email address
    • We occasionally work with external recruiting agencies. These partners will use legitimate business email addresses—never personal accounts like Gmail or Yahoo.
  • Our recruiting process will never ask you to provide financial or sensitive personal information, including but not limited to:
    • Social security or tax identification numbers
    • Credit card numbers
    • Bank account information

Diversity & Accommodations:

We're committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace—where people of all backgrounds, identities, experiences, and abilities are welcomed, valued, and supported. We recognize that there is no single path to success and embrace nontraditional career journeys and diverse perspectives as key to building stronger, more innovative teams.
We strive to ensure an inclusive experience throughout every stage of our hiring process and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations as needed. If you require accommodations or accessible formats at any point during our hiring process, please let your recruiter know.
As an equal opportunity employer our hiring process is designed to put you at ease and help you show your best work. If there’s anything we can do to improve your experience, we’re always open to feedback.

Privacy Notice:

If you apply for a job at Honeycomb and your application is unsuccessful (or you withdraw from the process or decline our offer), Honeycomb will retain your information after your application for a period of time in accordance with local laws. We retain this information for various reasons, including in case we face a legal challenge in respect of a recruitment decision, to consider you for other current or future jobs at Honeycomb, and to help us better understand, analyze and improve our recruitment processes.
For more information regarding our privacy practices please see the Honeycomb Privacy Notice.
If you do not want us to retain your information, or want us to update it, please contact . Please note, however, that we may retain some information if required by law or as necessary to protect ourselves from legal claims.

jobs.title: State System Partnerships Director
jobs.excerpt: About Empower Community Care Empower Community Care is a family of mission-driven organizations delivering evidence-based behavioral health, child welfare, and community care programs and services.
jobs.description:
About Empower Community Care

Empower Community Care is a family of mission-driven organizations delivering evidence-based behavioral health, child welfare, and community care programs and services. Our portfolio includes BSFT, Carey Group, Evidence-Based Associates (EBA), FFT LLC, MST Services, Orbis, and The Incredible Years — each advancing outcomes for children, families, and the communities we serve.

The Opportunity

Empower Community Care partners with public systems to deliver and scale evidence-based programs and services that improve outcomes for children, youth and families across juvenile justice, child welfare, behavioral health, human services and early childhood. Our portfolio brings together clinical programs, assessment and case management tools, practitioner development, implementation support and technology under one enterprise.
We are building a commercial organization capable of multiplying the company's reach over the next five years. The Director, State System Partnerships is central to that build. This role owns a named book of state-system relationships in a defined pod territory and is accountable for developing multi-program, multi-year partnerships with the agencies and executives who fund and govern care.
This is not a product sales role. You will sell Empower's ability to help a state understand need, select the right interventions, build local provider capacity and sustain outcomes. Your job is to orchestrate Empower's capabilities around the customer rather than to personally hold every one of them.

What Makes an Opportunity Enterprise

We define enterprise by the buyer's authority and the scope of the system conversation, not by deal size. This distinction matters, because it determines what you will be held accountable for.
  • Buyer authority: The buyer holds authority across multiple programs or agencies, not a single program budget.
  • Conversation scope: The conversation centers on system-level or population-level outcomes: juvenile justice transformation, family preservation, statewide behavioral health capacity.
  • Contract potential: There is a plausible path to a multi-year, multi-program contract vehicle.
  • Required fluency: The sale requires policy, funding and executive fluency.
A single-program engagement can be a large contract without being an enterprise sale, and a governor's office conversation can start small in dollar terms while functioning as an enterprise sale because of the multi-program access it opens. Where a buyer's authority stops at one program, our Specialty sellers lead and you support.

The Profile We Are Looking For

The strongest fit understands government from the inside and enterprise selling from the outside. That often looks like someone who began their career as a legislative staffer, in a governor’s policy office, in a state agency or in an appropriations role, and then moved to the commercial side of government services. It can equally look like someone who held a meaningful operating or policy role inside a state system and went on to build a successful track record selling into those systems.
We are looking for policy fluency, not policy ownership. You need to recognize and shape an opportunity, read appropriations and procurement dynamics, and hold your own with a commissioner, a Medicaid leader or a governor’s policy advisor. You are not expected to be our policy or government affairs expert. That capability sits with our government relations resources and executive leadership, and you will draw on it.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Named Account Book

  • Account ownership: Own a defined book of state and system relationships within an assigned pod territory, concentrated in Empower's priority states.
  • Account planning: Build and maintain an annual account plan for each priority state covering the systems and executives in play, continuum gaps, current Empower penetration, funding and procurement cycles, required proof points and the plays for the year.
  • Commercial accountability: Carry full commercial responsibility for the book: pipeline development, forecast accuracy, deal execution and renewal of the accounts you own.
  • CRM discipline: Maintain disciplined opportunity, forecast and activity hygiene in HubSpot. Pipeline that is not in the system does not exist.

Lead Complex Public-Sector Sales Cycles

  • Full sales lifecycle: Run the full enterprise lifecycle with state and local government, from first executive engagement through contract execution, on cycles that commonly run 12 to 24 months or longer.
  • Procurement navigation: Navigate multi-stakeholder procurement, braided funding, legislative calendars and agency leadership transitions.
  • Pre-positioning: Pre-position ahead of procurement: build relationships early enough to inform scope and requirements before an RFP is released.
  • Funding fluency: Bring funding fluency to the table. Understand how Title IV-E, Medicaid, CCBHC, JJDPA and state appropriations move through systems, and help buyers find budget where they believe none exists.
  • Government relations partnership: Draw on Empower's government relations strategists, lobbyists and executive leadership where policy positioning, legislative timing or appropriations advocacy can open or accelerate an opportunity. Policy ownership sits with those resources; you bring the fluency to recognize when to engage them and what to ask for.
  • Field intelligence: Translate field intelligence into clear direction for that partnership: which states, which committees, which budget cycles and which policy windows matter most to the book.

Sell the Empower Platform, Starting with Implementation and Quality Infrastructure

  • Primary seller: Act as the primary seller of Empower's implementation and quality infrastructure services: system assessment and readiness, technical assistance, provider capacity building, training, service coordination, workforce and program implementation.
  • Integrated positioning: Position the full portfolio to system-level buyers as an integrated capability rather than a catalog of programs.
  • Statewide continuum: Develop statewide continuum opportunities that connect assessment, intervention, practitioner development and outcomes measurement into a single partnership.
  • New buyer types: Expand into newer buyer types, including Medicaid agencies, managed care organizations and performance-based or value-based arrangements.

Run the Land-and-Expand Motion with Specialty and Customer Success

  • Create the mandate: Create the mandate at the system level, then bring in the relevant Specialty seller to lead the program or solution conversation with the operational buyer. On a genuine enterprise opportunity you stay actively engaged through close — you own the executive relationship and the procurement path while Specialty owns the solution.
  • Clean routing: Route cleanly to Specialty when qualification shows the buyer's authority stops at a single program. That is the model working, not a lost deal. You are measured on routing accurately and quickly, not on holding volume that belongs elsewhere.
  • Multi-seller coordination: Coordinate multiple Specialty sellers on multi-program pursuits and own the integrated proposal.
  • Capability orchestration: Orchestrate the full set of Empower capabilities around the account — clinical programs, assessment and practitioner tools, implementation support, government relations and executive sponsorship — rather than carrying every capability yourself.
  • Proof-point reinvestment: Carry delivery proof and outcomes evidence from initial engagements back up into the executive relationship to unlock the next program, region or agency.
  • Account ownership model: Own the system-level relationship, executive access and long-term contract strategy. Specialty owns program-level delivery and fidelity. Customer Success and Implementation Success owns adoption and implementation health. You are accountable for holding the whole account picture together.
  • Post-close transition: Transition program-level delivery relationships to Specialty, Customer Success, and Implementation Success after close. You retain the system relationship, the executive sponsor and the expansion strategy; you do not hold the operational day-to-day.
  • Renewal ownership: Stay engaged post-close. You own the renewal forecast and the expansion thesis for your accounts.

Represent Empower in the Market

  • Brand leadership: Lead with Empower Community Care in introductions, at conferences, and in written and digital presence. Program brands lead where eligibility criteria, evidence ratings or procurement language require it. Empower leads when we are being remembered; the program leads when we are being evaluated.
  • Industry presence: Build presence within relevant associations, coalitions and policy forums, and represent and exhibit Empower at regional and national events.
  • Market intelligence: Monitor legislative, regulatory and funding developments across your states and translate them into timed opportunities.
  • Feedback loop: Feed market intelligence, competitive insight and customer signal back to the Chief Growth Officer.

Accounts in Transition

Some accounts in this territory carry long-standing relationships held by our current Enterprise sellers. An early priority is to work directly with those colleagues to understand each account's history, relationship map, prior commitments and open threads, and to take on ownership through a deliberate, documented transition rather than a cold start. Protecting continuity in these relationships is part of the job, not an onboarding formality.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Ten or more years of combined public-sector, government or policy, and enterprise commercial selling experience, with demonstrated success owning and closing complex state-system opportunities. We are deliberately open on how those years are distributed; substantial time inside government followed by a strong commercial record is a welcome profile.
  • Track record: A track record of closing multi-year public-sector contracts with system-level buyers, not only program-level purchases, and of owning a multi-state or statewide book.
  • Sector depth: Substantive experience in one or more of our systems: juvenile justice, child welfare, behavioral health, human services, Medicaid or education.
  • Procurement command: Command of government procurement, contracting vehicles and public funding mechanisms.
  • Policy fluency: Policy and funding fluency: the ability to read legislative, appropriations and budget cycles and time commercial strategy against them.
  • Executive credibility: Credibility and composure with senior public officials, and the judgment to navigate agency politics with discretion.
  • Cross-functional orchestration: Demonstrated ability to orchestrate cross-functional pursuit teams and internal capabilities without direct authority.
  • Travel: Willingness to travel regionally and nationally.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Evidence-based selling: Experience selling evidence-based programs, clinical models or outcomes-based services.
  • Existing relationships: Existing relationships with system leaders in the assigned territory's priority states.
  • Value-based contracting: Experience with managed care, Medicaid or value-based contracting.
  • Government relations collaboration: Experience working alongside government relations, advocacy or lobbying teams as part of a commercial strategy.
  • Public-sector background: Direct service inside a state system: agency, legislature, governor's office, appropriations or a comparable public role.
  • Matrixed orgs: Experience in a multi-brand or matrixed commercial organization, and comfort operating in one being actively built.

Core Competencies

  • Enterprise and consultative selling into complex public systems
  • Account planning and long-cycle opportunity orchestration
  • Policy- and funding-informed commercial strategy
  • Executive communication and presence
  • Cross-functional leadership without direct authority
  • Forecast discipline and CRM rigor
  • Comfort with ambiguity and appetite to help build the model, not just work inside it

Additional Requirements

  • Background Check: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, consistent with applicable law and Empower's standard hiring practices.
  • Confidentiality: This role may involve exposure to confidential organizational, financial, program, and government-relationship information, including procurement-sensitive and funding-strategy communications. The employee must maintain strict confidentiality and comply with Empower's internal data governance and confidentiality policies.
  • Work Environment: This is a remote position based within the assigned pod territory, requiring prolonged periods of computer- and video-conferencing-based work, along with travel of approximately 25% of the time, regional and national, for in-person meetings, conferences, and government-partner engagements. Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the ADA.
  • Other Duties: This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Benefits

Empower Community Care offers a competitive total-rewards package, which includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement savings; paid time off and holidays; and life insurance.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As Staff Product Manager, Test & Code Coverage, you'll build product capabilities from initial discovery through launch and adoption. You'll help engineering teams understand why pipelines fail, improve test automation, and use code coverage to make better decisions about software quality and risk.

You'll turn a technically complex problem space into a focused strategy, roadmap, and developer experience. Working closely with Engineering and Design, you'll explore how agents can diagnose failures, recommend next steps, and help teams recover safely. The goal isn't to add artificial intelligence (AI) for its own sake. It's to reduce manual work and help developers get back to a safe, shippable state without losing trust or control.

At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. You'll contribute to that mission by making testing and coverage insights more useful across the software development lifecycle.

What you'll do

  • Define and communicate the Test & Code Coverage product vision, strategy, and outcome-focused roadmap, from discovery through a minimum viable product, beta, launch, and continued iteration.
  • Identify customer problems across pipeline failure diagnosis, test automation, test optimization, code coverage, and recovery. Build the case for investment, prioritize foundational and customer-facing work, and reshape or stop initiatives that aren't creating value.
  • Work with Engineering to understand pipeline failures caused by flaky tests, testing gaps, environment issues, configuration problems, and coverage blind spots. Connect code changes, tests, pipeline behavior, historical patterns, and risk to help developers find a diagnosis and an actionable next step.
  • Work directly with customers to understand how they author, maintain, select, prioritize, and debug tests. Connect test selection, test impact analysis, code coverage, and pipeline intelligence to reduce flaky tests, shorten feedback loops, and focus testing effort where it lowers the most risk.
  • Partner with Engineering and Design to prototype agent-driven workflows for failure diagnosis, test authoring and repair, optimization, coverage analysis, and recovery. Make actions reviewable through evidence, confidence, human approval, and safe paths to propose code changes and merge requests. Use AI tools in your own product work to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and accelerate learning.
  • Define and measure outcomes such as time to diagnose, time to recover, failure recurrence, test signal quality, and developer confidence. Validate problems and solutions with customers and learn from production usage.
  • Partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing to connect testing insights with code review, pipelines, and release decisions. Turn customer evidence into clear narratives that support adoption and future investment.
  • Lead through clear written communication, prioritization, and product judgment. Influence senior stakeholders, establish repeatable discovery and measurement practices, and mentor other product managers.

What you'll bring

  • Experience owning complex technical products, platforms, or developer workflows at Staff, Senior Staff, Principal, or equivalent scope, including building a new product or capability from initial validation through launch and adoption.
  • Strong product fundamentals in customer discovery, problem framing, prioritization, roadmap development, outcome measurement, and iterative delivery.
  • Technical fluency in one or more relevant areas, such as software testing, test automation, code coverage, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), developer tools, DevOps, developer experience, quality engineering, or software delivery.
  • An understanding of how engineering teams build, test, review, and ship software, and the ability to work with engineers on test architecture, pipeline behavior, code changes, data, integrations, reliability, and scale.
  • Experience diagnosing technical problems and turning complex, noisy signals into clear user experiences and actionable workflows.
  • Experience exploring AI or agent-driven solutions for developer workflows, with the judgment to distinguish useful automation from unsafe or low-confidence actions.
  • Experience using customer conversations to understand problems and inform product decisions, communicating clearly in writing and conversation, and influencing across functions with shared ownership. You can work directly with developers, quality engineers, platform teams, engineering leaders, and executives, and move between strategy and implementation detail.

About the team

Our work brings together Product, Engineering, and Design, with input from Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing. We work directly with developers, quality engineers, and engineering leaders to understand their testing practices, validate ideas, and learn from how they use the product.

We give Engineering and Design clear customer context and room to shape solutions. Our decisions draw on customer evidence and measurable outcomes, and we revisit approaches that aren't creating value. You'll contribute to how we discover problems, prioritize work, and measure progress, as well as sharing product management practices with other product managers.

As part of GitLab's all-remote organization, we collaborate asynchronously across regions. Our work emphasizes transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.

About Us

We are looking for a senior developer who can take ownership of mobile development, deliver reliable software, and help our team become more effective at building applications with AI.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Mobile App Developer with strong Kotlin Multiplatform expertise and an excellent background in native Android development with Kotlin.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You will develop and improve our application, solve complex technical problems, and establish effective workflows for AI-assisted and agentic development. Experience with GPS, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Ultra-Wideband (UWB), or related location and proximity technologies would be particularly valuable.

You will also share your knowledge with our internal team, including mentoring a junior team member who is learning to build Android applications through AI-assisted development, often referred to as “vibe coding.”

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, maintain, and improve our Android application using Kotlin and Kotlin Multiplatform.
  • Design shared application logic and integrate it with platform-specific functionality.
  • Implement and troubleshoot location and proximity features involving GPS, BLE, UWB, and related device capabilities.
  • Address practical mobile challenges such as permissions, background execution, battery consumption, connectivity, and differences between devices.
  • Use AI coding assistants and coding agents extensively to implement features, investigate defects, refactor code, and support testing.
  • Set up and improve agentic development workflows, including task decomposition, project context, automated checks, and review processes.
  • Review and validate AI-generated code, taking responsibility for its correctness, maintainability, security, and performance.
  • Test relevant functionality on real devices and resolve problems that automated tests alone may not reveal.
  • Mentor our junior team member through practical demonstrations, pair programming, and understandable explanations.
  • Document important technical decisions and share reusable knowledge with the internal team.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated senior-level experience delivering and maintaining production Android applications with Kotlin.
  • Strong practical experience with Kotlin Multiplatform, including shared code, platform-specific integrations, and the boundaries between them.
  • Solid understanding of Android architecture, Jetpack Compose, coroutines, Flow, application lifecycle, and state management.
  • Strong debugging skills and the ability to investigate problems across application code, APIs, and device behavior.
  • Substantial hands-on experience using AI coding tools to deliver working software.
  • A strong interest in agentic coding and the ability to establish effective development workflows around coding agents.
  • The ability to assess AI-generated solutions critically and explain why an implementation is appropriate.
  • Willingness and ability to teach less experienced team members patiently and clearly.
  • The ability to work independently, communicate progress clearly, and take ownership of results in a remote team.
  • Interest in a long-term, full-time position and availability to start promptly after an agreement is reached.

Especially Valuable Experience

  • GPS positioning, location accuracy, sensor data, and proximity detection.
  • BLE discovery, advertising, connections, and signal-strength limitations.
  • UWB ranging, distance measurement, direction estimation, and hardware compatibility.
  • NFC and other device-to-device interactions.
  • Building automated development and testing workflows that combine human oversight with coding agents.

What We Offer

  • A fully remote, full-time role with a long-term perspective.
  • Compensation based on your experience, expertise, and responsibilities.
  • Ownership of meaningful mobile development work.
  • The opportunity to shape how our team uses AI and coding agents.
  • Close collaboration with an internal team that wants to learn from your experience.

Remote Working Arrangement

Our remote working setup includes a time-tracking tool that records mouse-click and keyboard-activity metrics and captures screenshots of the screen. This monitoring is part of the working arrangement and will be explained during the recruitment process.

Applicants should be comfortable working with this setup.

How to Apply

Please submit your CV and a short overview of relevant projects.

Include:

  • Your role in developing Android applications and Kotlin Multiplatform solutions.
  • Any practical experience with GPS, BLE, UWB, or similar technologies.
  • The AI coding tools and agentic workflows you use, with an example of how they helped you deliver a working application or feature.

Public portfolio or GitHub links are welcome where available.

About Semble

At Semble, we're on a mission to enable health professionals to amplify their impact. Our cloud-based clinical system helps thousands of healthcare professionals deliver better care through powerful, intuitive and secure software.

We're a passionate team united by three cultural drivers:

Impact – We do work that matters.

Collaboration – We are in it together.

Human touch – We care deeply.

We're also embracing AI, both in how we work and in the products we build. We're looking for people who share our curiosity about emerging technologies and are excited to explore their potential responsibly.

This role can be fully remote in the UK or France.

What you will be doing

As a Senior Product Designer within our Clinical team, you'll design experiences that support healthcare professionals in making decisions, documenting care and managing complex clinical workflows.

You'll work closely with Product Managers, Engineers and Clinical Safety specialists, balancing innovation with the responsibility of creating safe, reliable healthcare technology.

You'll also help evolve how our design team works, using AI and emerging technologies to explore ideas, learn faster and deliver better outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Own complex clinical design challenges – Lead design work from discovery through delivery, translating user needs, clinical requirements and technical constraints into intuitive, accessible solutions.

  • Embrace AI and emerging technologies – Use AI-assisted tools to accelerate research, exploration, prototyping and iteration, and identify opportunities for AI and automation to improve clinical workflows.

  • Facilitate collaborative problem-solving – Bring Product, Engineering and Clinical Safety together to explore opportunities, navigate different perspectives and reach well-informed decisions.
  • Conduct user research – Build relationships with healthcare professionals through interviews, field visits and usability testing, translating insights into meaningful product improvements.

What we are looking for

At this level, we expect you to work with a high degree of autonomy, independently owning complex design challenges and influence decisions beyond your immediate workstream.

We're looking for someone who combines strong design fundamentals with sound judgement, curiosity and a constructive approach to collaboration.

Key skills and experience

  • Complex, high-risk product experience – Proven experience designing clinical systems or similarly high-risk software, where errors can have significant consequences. Experience working alongside safety, risk or regulatory specialists.

  • Innovation and safety judgement – Ability to explore ambitious solutions while understanding risk, recognising trade-offs and knowing when a simpler, more predictable approach is appropriate.
  • Practical AI experience – A proven track record of using AI-assisted tools to improve your design workflow, with examples of how you've applied them to research, exploration, prototyping or delivery.
  • Research and product thinking – Experience conducting user research, navigating ambiguity and using evidence to make informed design decisions that deliver measurable outcomes.
  • Collaborative facilitation – Ability to bring people together, constructively challenge assumptions, welcome different perspectives and help teams move towards shared decisions.
  • Ownership and adaptability – Comfortable leading work independently, taking responsibility for outcomes, embracing feedback and continuously evolving your approach.

  • Experience designing AI-powered workflows, automation or intelligent decision-support experiences.

  • Autonomy and ownership – we’ll set the vision and share the context, then we trust you to run with things – that’s the reason we hire you!
