jobs.excerpt: Huron helps its clients drive growth, enhance performance and sustain leadership in the markets they serve.
jobs.description:
Huron helps its clients drive growth, enhance performance and sustain leadership in the markets they serve. We help healthcare organizations build innovation capabilities and accelerate key growth initiatives, enabling organizations to own the future, instead of being disrupted by it. Together, we empower clients to create sustainable growth, optimize internal processes and deliver better consumer outcomes.

Health systems, hospitals and medical clinics are under immense pressure to improve clinical outcomes and reduce the cost of providing patient care. Investing in new partnerships, clinical services and technology is not enough to create meaningful and substantive change. To succeed long-term, healthcare organizations must empower leaders, clinicians, employees, affiliates and communities to build cultures that foster innovation to achieve the best outcomes for patients.

Joining the Huron team means you’ll help our clients evolve and adapt to the rapidly changing healthcare environment and optimize existing business operations, improve clinical outcomes, create a more consumer-centric healthcare experience, and drive physician, patient and employee engagement across the enterprise.

Join our team as the expert you are now and create your future.

Embark on a dynamic journey as a Senior Lead Software Engineer with the Care Insights team, shaping the future of healthcare analytics. In this role, you'll lead the development of cutting-edge analytics products, collaborating closely with product leadership to craft strategies and roadmaps that drive growth.
Dive into the heart of data innovation, designing ETL processes, maintaining pipelines, and leveraging statistical and machine learning algorithms for impactful data analysis and visualization. This role offers exposure to a spectrum of technologies—from relational databases like MySQL to Python, R, and Cloud Services (AWS). Collaborate seamlessly in a Git-powered, collaborative software development environment.

As you engage your passion for learning and professional growth, mentor junior team members and thrive in a positive, team-centric environment. Become a catalyst for innovation, contributing to the enhancement of patient outcomes by analyzing millions of daily Electronic Health Record (EHR) records.
If you're a self-starter eager to make a meaningful impact and shape the landscape of healthcare analytics, this opportunity is for you. Join us on a journey where your skills and strengths will play a pivotal role in driving innovation and growth within the realm of healthcare analytics.

As a Senior Lead Software Engineer, in the Clinical Insights team, your daily responsibilities will revolve around leading the development of healthcare analytics products. Day-to-day tasks include designing and maintaining ETL processes for data transformation, managing data pipelines and databases, and creating data visualizations and dashboards. Additionally, you will implement statistical and machine learning algorithms, staying abreast of tech trends, and mentoring junior team members. If you are comfortable with relational databases, proficient in Python, R, or equivalent languages, and have a solid grasp of web frameworks, this role offers the opportunity to drive innovation in healthcare analytics and contribute to the enhancement of patient outcomes.

Responsibilities:

As a Senior Lead Software Engineer at Huron, you will lead the development of healthcare analytics products. Your role involves designing efficient ETL processes, optimizing data pipelines, and ensuring seamless technology integration within a small, focused team comprised of PHDs, Engineers, Product Managers and Consultants.

Collaborating closely with this cross functional team, you will drive innovation and explore advancements to stay at the forefront of technology offerings. Your strategic contributions extend to optimizing development workflows and guiding decisions to enhance overall efficiency both in the team and at client organizations.

Measuring the impact of analytics products, you will utilize appropriate tools to showcase value in patient outcomes and client organizational objectives. In summary, your role is instrumental in the strategic development, optimization, and impactful decision-making within the realm of healthcare analytics at Huron.

Required:

  • U.S. work authorization is required.
  • B.S. degree with a focus in in computer science, information systems, engineering and/or equivalent work experience.
  • 5 + years of relevant software development experience and/or along with leading a project or team.
  • Proven experience as a Senior Software Engineer, demonstrating expertise in leading the development of analytics products or similar.
  • Proficiency in relational database concepts, with a preference for MySQL.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, R, or equivalent languages.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively in team-based environments with a positive and supportive demeanor.
  • Competence in maintaining data pipelines and databases.
  • Capability for autonomous work as a self-starter.
  • This position can be Full Time remote and located anywhere within the U.S.
  • Potential to travel up to 10% annually.

Preferred:

  • Agile development process experience with Scrum preferred.
  • Familiarity with Unix-like operating systems, particularly Linux.
  • Experience designing ETL processes for data transformation.
  • Basic understanding of large-scale data warehousing technologies and tools.
  • Expertise with Cloud Services, preferably AWS.

The estimated base salary for this job is $140,000 - $190,000 USD. The range represents a good faith estimate of the range that Huron reasonably expects to pay for this job at the time of the job posting. The actual salary paid to an individual will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to specific skills or certifications, years of experience, market changes, and required travel. This job is also eligible to participate in Huron’s annual incentive compensation program, which reflects Huron’s pay for performance philosophy. Inclusive of annual incentive compensation opportunity, the total estimated compensation range for this job is $168,000 - $228,000 USD. The job is also eligible to participate in Huron’s benefit plans which include medical, dental and vision coverage and other wellness programs. The salary range information provided is in accordance with applicable state and local laws regarding salary transparency that are currently in effect and may be implemented in the future.

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are BioMarin is a leading rare disease biotechnology company focused on genetically defined conditions.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

BioMarin is a leading rare disease biotechnology company focused on genetically defined conditions.

Guided by our purpose to develop medicines that make a profound impact on people’s lives, our global teams have delivered a portfolio of therapies since our founding in 1997. Our revolutionary treatments for conditions like achondroplasia (the most common form of dwarfism), PKU (phenylketonuria), CLN2, a form of Batten disease, and a number of forms of MPS (mucopolysaccharidosis) offer new possibilities for patients and families who previously had few, if any, available options. More recently, with the close of the Amicus acquisition, our portfolio has expanded to include therapies for Fabry disease and Pompe disease, expanding our ability to reach more people living with rare genetic conditions.

Our success comes from our unwavering commitment to excellence, our deep understanding of patient needs, our scientific expertise, and our world-class manufacturing capabilities. At the heart of BioMarin is a dedicated team of the brightest minds in the industry working together to deliver innovative therapies to patients and families around the world.

About Worldwide Research and Development

From research and discovery to post-market clinical development, our R&D engine involves all bench and clinical research and the associated groups that support those endeavors. Our teams work on developing first-in-class and best-in-class therapeutics that provide meaningful advances to patients who live with rare diseases.

enior Medical Director, Clinical Science (Neuromuscular Disease)

BioMarin is the world leader in delivering therapeutics that provide meaningful advances to patients who live with serious and life-threatening rare genetic diseases. We target diseases that lack effective therapies and affect relatively small numbers of patients, many of whom are children. These conditions are often inherited, difficult to diagnose, progressively debilitating and have few, if any, treatment options. BioMarin will continue to focus on advancing therapies that are the first or best of their kind.

BioMarin’s Research & Development group is responsible for everything from research and discovery to post-market clinical development. Research & Development involves all bench and clinical research and the associated groups that support those endeavors. Our teams work on developing first-in-class and best-in-class therapeutics that provide meaningful advances to patients who live with rare diseases. Come join our team and make a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.

Scope:

BioMarin Pharmaceutical seeks a M.D./PhD with suitable background and experience in the biotech/pharma industry (or related) to join a multidisciplinary clinical research team and oversee clinical trial execution and output. The Senior Medical Director will support the global clinical development team investigating novel potential treatments. They will support the strategic development and execution of the global clinical development plan including the opportunity to participate in global regulatory filing activities. Experience with rare diseases would be advantageous.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead preparation of clinical sections of all relevant regulatory filings (IND, study reports, NDA, etc.), especially BLA filing experience highly desired
  • Lead strategic planning and execution of clinical trials
  • Provide clinical expertise for the research and development projects under their care; lead clinical science aspects of regulatory filings
  • Serve as the Medical Monitor for clinical trials; participate in management of studies and serve as expert on clinical and medical issues to other colleagues and study site staff
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders (Project Management, Clinical Operations, Regulatory, Medical Affairs, translational science, data science, Commercial, CMC etc) to ensure successful management of the project
  • Build relationships with and collaborate with investigators and key opinion leaders to ensure implementation of latest clinical thinking and guidelines into the clinical development plan
  • Serve as medical and technical resource for clinical issues raised by internal and external collaborators, investigators, consultants and contract resources; participate in the pharmacovigilance reporting process
  • Assist in clinical project and protocol development in general; provide ongoing medical input into study documentation, e.g. source data verification plans, case report form design etc
  • Attend and provide scientific and medical support for investigator meetings
  • Participate in analysis and interpretation of interim and final study data with internal colleagues and external investigators
  • Participate in the writing of final study reports and lead the data dissemination plan for projects under their care; including development of publications, abstracts, and presentations; represent the company at scientific meetings
  • Support other functions within the organization as appropriate; this may include business development activities, science projects

Experience:

  • Relevant experience in pharmaceutical/biotech or related industries. For appointment at the Senior Medical Director level a minimum of 5 years relevant experience is required
  • Outstanding leadership, presentation, written and oral communication skills required
  • Collaborative and flexible in interactions at all levels within the company, and with external collaborators
  • Ability to work proactively and effectively, with exceptional creative problem-solving skills
  • Excellent strategic planning, organizational, analytical and communication skills
  • Knowledgeable and current in GCP guidelines in US and Europe; regulatory filing experience would be advantageous
  • Be well connected within the medical and scientific community and have a proven successful track record
  • Experience in rare diseases is desirable.

Education:

  • MD, MD/PhD, PhD

jobs.title: Associate
jobs.excerpt: About SNV Proximate What if you could combine the commercial rigour of consulting, investment, or corporate strategy with the opportunity to create meaningful development impact at scale?
jobs.description:
About SNV Proximate
What if you could combine the commercial rigour of consulting, investment, or corporate strategy with the opportunity to create meaningful development impact at scale? SNV’s newly established impact capital accelerator aims to do exactly that: develop commercially viable solutions that generate both business value and development impact. Combining expertise in impact-driven finance and inclusive commercial value chains, SNV Proximate will operate with the pace, ambition, and commercial mindset of a boutique advisory firm while leveraging the reach, credibility, and market presence of a global development organisation.

Working with companies, investors, development finance institutions, foundations, and governments, this is your chance to join the team that will design, test, and grow new approaches to mobilising investment, strengthening markets, and building more inclusive and resilient value chains across emerging economies. It is a place for people who are excited by building something new, comfortable operating across both commercial and development environments, and motivated by turning ambitious ideas into scalable results.

Position overview
SNV is building a commercial markets accelerator, which runs client engagements across two streams — impact-driven finance (IDF) and inclusive commercial value chains (ICVC). Associates are the delivery backbone of both. This role sits at the intersection of substantive client work and internal knowledge building — you will contribute to billable engagements, work directly with clients in the field and in meetings, and help build the evidence base that sharpens the offer over time.

This is an early-career role designed for someone with 3–5 years of experience who has done solid analytical work and is ready to take on more client-facing responsibility. You will work across both IDF and ICVC engagements, mentored by stream leads, with the expectation that you develop a meaningful specialism in one stream over time.

The Accelerator is small and the work is varied. In any given month you might be building a financial model for an impact fund client, conducting field interviews with smallholder farmers, drafting a chapter of a market systems report, or packaging an internal case study for BD use. You will not be siloed.

Who you are
You are a motivated, curious, and analytical professional who enjoys tackling complex challenges and turning insights into action. You combine strong analytical skills with sound judgement, including knowing when to use AI and when a more human-centred approach is needed.

You thrive in fast-paced environments and enjoy working across different workstreams rather than specialising in a single sector or vertical. Adaptable and commercially minded, you are excited by opportunities to create both business value and development impact.

As an Associate, you contribute to both winning and delivering client mandates through high-quality analysis, research, stakeholder engagement, and problem-solving. You structure complex problems effectively, identify the key insights and implications, and translate mandates into practical recommendations and deliverables. Your work is accurate, well-reasoned, and thoroughly checked, requiring minimal rework and giving managers confidence in your output.

You act on feedback quickly, keep stakeholders informed, meet deadlines, and proactively flag risks or challenges. Over time, you take on increasingly complex assignments, require less guidance, and build a reputation as a trusted colleague whose expertise and collaboration make clients and peers eager to work with you again.

Key Responsibilities

Client engagement delivery

  • Contribute substantively to client engagements as a core delivery resource — research, analysis, data collection, and drafting, to a standard that requires minimal rework by the delivery lead.
  • Conduct primary research: stakeholder interviews, field visits, surveys, and focus groups. Travel to project geographies is a standard part of this role.
  • Synthesise secondary research: literature reviews, market assessments, policy analysis, and competitor landscape reviews.
  • Build and maintain financial models, data trackers, and analytical frameworks to the level required by the engagement.
  • Draft sections of client reports, slide decks, and working papers — presenting findings clearly and at a level of quality appropriate for external audiences.
  • Participate in client meetings and workshops where appropriate — presenting analysis, facilitating sessions, and taking structured notes.

Stream-specific work

  • Associates are generalists across both streams, with the expectation of developing a specialism in one. The lists below illustrates what the work looks like in each stream.
  • IDF stream tasks
    • Landscape analysis of impact investment opportunities in a specific sector or geography.
    • Financial modelling for blended finance structures — grant/concessional capital ratios, return scenarios, investor waterfall analysis.
    • Due diligence research on investees or TA recipients — financial performance, impact track record, operational capacity.
    • Impact indicator development and data collection for investor reporting (IRIS+, IMP frameworks).
    • Market sizing and pipeline development analysis for fund managers or DFIs.
    • Synthesis of portfolio-level impact data across multiple investees into consolidated investor reports.
  • ICVC stream tasks
    • Value chain mapping and diagnostic analysis — identifying bottlenecks, margin distribution, and inclusion gaps.
    • Smallholder farmer interviews and household-level data collection and analysis.
    • Market systems analysis — mapping actors, incentives, and constraints across a commodity or sector.
    • Business case development for inclusive sourcing or supply chain investment, including financial modelling.
    • Competitive landscape reviews for agribusiness clients entering new markets or commodities.
    • Supplier development programme design — segmentation, needs assessment, and service delivery modelling.
    • Policy and regulatory environment analysis for government advisory engagements.

Internal knowledge and BD support

  • Contribute to the internal knowledge base — producing case studies, evidence summaries, and sector briefs from completed engagements. This feeds directly into the sales collateral and proposal infrastructure. Work produced here has a commercial use, not just an archival one.
  • Support the Senior Manager for Impact and Intelligence with cross-portfolio data collection and analysis.
  • Contribute to BD collateral where relevant: sector evidence packs, market data, and proof points for pitch materials.
  • Support proposal development with research, data, and analysis sections — not writing the proposal, but providing the evidence infrastructure. Proposal support is a regular part of this role, not an occasional one. The unit cannot win work without strong analytical inputs to bids.

What you bring

To be considered for this role, you bring:

  • 3–5 years of experience in research, analytical, or advisory role — in consulting, development finance, agribusiness, international development, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience producing high-quality analytical outputs that were used in client-facing or decision-making contexts.
  • Experience conducting primary research — interviews, surveys, or field data collection — in emerging market or development contexts.
  • Some exposure to either IDF or ICVC subject matter: impact investing, blended finance, value chain development, agribusiness, or market systems.
  • Experience working across multiple projects or workstreams simultaneously.

Additionally, we value:

  • Strong analytical skills — quantitative and qualitative. Comfortable building financial models and analysing large datasets as well as synthesising interview findings and qualitative evidence.
  • Clear, concise written English to publication standard. You can write a crisp executive summary, a well-structured analytical section, and a compelling slide — and they do not all sound the same.
  • Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint at a working level. Experience with data analysis tools (R, Python, Stata, or equivalent) an advantage.
  • Intellectual curiosity about the sectors we work in. You read beyond the brief.
  • English required. French or Portuguese a strong advantage.
  • Reporting line: Director
  • Location: Flexible.We welcome applications from candidates based anywhere within the time zones spanning Ghana to Singapore. As this role involves international collaboration and travel, candidates should be located within reasonable reach of a well-connected international airport.
  • Travel requirements: International travel will be required.
  • Expected start date: November/December 2026

What we offer
We offer a unique opportunity to help build and shape a new venture from the ground up, working alongside a diverse and experienced global team. You will have significant autonomy, exposure to senior leaders and clients, and the opportunity to influence how the Accelerator grows and operates.
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, with compensation determined based on relevant experience, skills, and internal equity.

Contract arrangements
As a globally flexible role, employment arrangements will be aligned with the successful candidate's location and applicable local regulations. Further details will be discussed with shortlisted candidates during the recruitment process.

Working at SNV
At SNV we challenge and inspire and offer continuous growth. We offer meaningful opportunities to shape the future, expand your skills, and collaborate with a vibrant, global network of experts. At SNV your contribution matter, and your development is our priority.

We are home to 57 cultures working in 22 countries, with about 95% of our team members holding the nationality of the respective countries we work in. We promote international career development. Our workforce consists of a mix of both people with longstanding tenure, willing to share their institutional knowledge, as well as people with local expertise and knowledge. All with an inquisitive view and united in ‘ONE SNV’ working towards our purpose.

Together, we are committed to the effective and efficient stewardship of resources and maximising positive, lasting impacts. Our ability to deliver results rests on our robust foundation of experience, technical knowledge, evidence and learning; our commitment to strengthening capacities and catalysing partnerships; and the relationships and trust of those we work alongside.

SNV is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment and make recruitment decisions based on merit, competence, and organisational needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, nationality, marital status, or any other status protected by applicable law. Women, persons with disabilities, and candidates from under-represented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

How to apply
If you meet the key requirements and feel inspired by this opportunity, we warmly welcome your application. Please submit your CV and motivation letter by 29th of October via SmartRecruiters.

To ensure a focused and respectful recruitment process, we kindly ask that you apply only if you meet the essential qualifications and are available to work in the specified location.
Please note that only candidates progressing to the next stage of the selection process will be contacted. Individual feedback cannot be provided.

If this role isn’t the right fit but you’re interested in joining SNV in the future, we invite you to follow us on LinkedIn and our career page Vacancies | SNV to stay updated on new opportunities that match your profile.

Reference and vetting check
At SNV, our belief in the CARE principles — Commitment to impact, Adaptive to Context, Respecting Difference and Expertise in Practice — shapes how we work with each other and every interaction we have with our colleagues, partners, and the communities we serve. These values guide how we welcome new team members, ensuring our workplace remains a place of trust, safety, and dignity for all.

As part of our commitment to a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, we carry out reference and background checks for all determined positions, with particular attention to safeguarding. You will be invited to provide the contact details of [two] referees, and we will only approach them once you have given your permission. We handle this process with care, empathy, and strict confidentiality, using the information solely for purposes related to your application and the role you have applied for.

SNV is committed to safeguarding and to protecting children and adults from all forms of harm, with zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, or any other form of misconduct. As part of creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive working environment, all staff, consultants, and partners are expected to uphold SNV’s safeguarding, child protection, ethical standards, and CARE principles. In line with these commitments — and as a participant in the Inter‑Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS) — SNV will request a Statement of Conduct from your previous employer(s), covering any substantiated findings of misconduct, to ensure a recruitment process that safeguards and protect the communities we serve.

Senior Product Manager

Handbooks, Compliance Learning, and Multi-State Compliance

Workforce Compliance | Reports to: Senior Director, Product Management | Mitratech US

At Mitratech, we are a team of innovators focused on building world-class products that simplify operations in the Legal, Risk, Compliance, and HR functions. We are a close-knit, globally dispersed team that thrives in an ecosystem that supports individual excellence and takes pride in its diverse and inclusive work culture centered around great people practices, learning opportunities, and having fun! Our culture is the ideal blend of entrepreneurial spirit and enterprise investment, enabling the chance to move at a rapid pace with some of the most complex, leading-edge technologies available.

For over 35 years, the experts at Mitratech have been focused on solving the complex needs. Today, we serve 20,000 client companies of all sizes globally, representing 30% of the Fortune 500 and over 500,000 users in over 160 countries.

As we continue to grow, we're always looking for resourceful, enthusiastic, and fresh perspectives. Join our global team and see what makes Mitratech a truly exceptional place to work!

About the Team

Mitratech Workforce Compliance turns constantly changing labor and employment law into a strategic advantage for US employers of every size. Our ARIES Intelligence Core combines an expert-curated labor law corpus, agentic AI, and certified HR experts to assure compliance everywhere employment law introduces risk: every law, every policy, every employee, from sourcing to termination. We reach employers directly and through partners, including brokers, carriers, PEOs, and HCM and payroll platforms.

This role sits on our newly formed Workforce Compliance product team. The team exists to own the customer problem end to end: understanding the buyer, the user, the approver, and the accountable owner behind every compliance job, and shaping one coherent product direction across the portfolio. We build once on shared intelligence and reusable capabilities, we lean on licensed experts for judgment, and we hold ourselves to evidence over opinion. Product managers here decide within their scope, raise concerns while they are still small, and communicate clearly so that decisions get made faster.

Job Overview

Mitratech is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the customer problem of keeping a growing, multi-location workforce compliant with the policies, notices, and training the law requires. Your primary products are Handbooks and compliance learning. Your workflow scope covers Multi-State and Jurisdiction Management and Onboarding, excluding I-9 and E-Verify, which is owned by peera.

Multi-state compliance and handbook confusion is the single largest theme in our customer and prospect conversations today. Employers who built a business in one state and expanded to three do not know what changed, usually find out after a mistake, and are maintaining a handbook by copy and paste. Brokers and PEOs who deliver that handbook under their own brand cannot always prove it is current or that it is being used. Employees rarely see or acknowledge the policies that protect both sides. Producing a compliant handbook today is time consuming and often requires rounds of revision. We believe that the process should be efficient and that delivering insights to the right system or person at the right time should be paramount.

You will own that problem across every channel we sell through: our own product, partner platforms, chat, and authorized agents calling our Intelligence Core. You will decide which customer journeys come first, what the shared handbook engine must do, how policy changes flow into acknowledgments, training assignments, and downstream HR and payroll settings, and how we prove the outcome to the employer and to the partner who sponsored it.

What you will own

  • Handbooks: intake, policy selection and assembly from verified content, multi-state and section-level editing, review and human approval, versioning, publication, and portability of the employer's handbook across sponsor and broker changes
  • Learn and Compliance Learning: mandated training (harassment prevention, safety, and similar) assigned and tracked against the jurisdictions where employees actually work, and the proof of completion that goes with it
  • Multi-State and Jurisdiction Management: the employer's jurisdiction footprint as a shared, reusable input that triggers the right policies, notices, training, and alerts when a workforce crosses a state line or a headcount threshold
  • Onboarding (excluding I-9 and E-Verify): new-hire state reporting, wage theft prevention notices, and handbook and policy acknowledgment at hire and at every policy update
  • The post-approval loop: distribution to employees, acknowledgment tracking, manager guidance, and a human-reviewed handoff of policy changes to payroll and HRIS configuration
  • How these experiences show up inside partner platforms and through the Intelligence Core API, with attribution that travels with our content

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Own the customer problem

  • Be the person in the company who knows the most about how a multi-location employer, an HR generalist, a broker account manager, and a PEO team actually keep policies and training current today, and where that work breaks
  • Maintain a living view of buyer, user, approver, and accountable owner for each job in your scope, across direct and partner channels
  • Set the outcomes we are aiming for (for example, time to a publishable handbook, share of employees acknowledged, training completion against mandate deadlines) and hold the team to them

Lead customer discovery

  • Run a continuous discovery cadence: weekly conversations with employers, HR practitioners, brokers, PEOs, and our own HR experts, plus regular review of sales and support call evidence
  • Turn what you learn into explicit, testable assumptions. Label what we know, what we assume, and what the evidence supports
  • Collaborate with Product Design to validate solutions with prototypes and small experiments before committing engineering capacity, and be willing to kill ideas the evidence does not support
  • Partner with the persona and research work already underway so the team shares one picture of the customer instead of several

Shape AI-native experiences with experts in the loop

  • Design handbook and training experiences with our Foundations counterparts that gather employer context once, apply cited guidance and expert review, coordinate the approved facts into the document, the acknowledgment, and the training assignment, and prove completion
  • Define where an agent can act, where a human must approve, and where a question routes to a licensed expert.
  • Work with the Intelligence Core team so your experiences draw on the shared labor law corpus and employer context rather than duplicating intelligence

Deliver and measure

  • Write product requirement documents and decision documents that engineering, design, and content experts can act on. Prioritize the backlog and own launch and adoption
  • Define the metrics that show whether the customer problem is actually getting solved, instrument them, and report on them plainly
  • Protect current customer and partner commitments while shaping the next plan, and surface conflicts early

Work across the company

  • Partner with engineering, design, data science, the compliance content team, HR advisory experts, customer success, partner management, and go-to-market
  • Give partners a clear story for how Handbooks and Learn add value in their channel and how they can prove utilization to their own clients
  • Enable sales, support, and implementation on what you ship and why it matters to the employer

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

  • You have interviewed dozens of employers, practitioners, and partners and produced a synthesis the whole team uses to prioritize
  • The handbook production cycle is measurably shorter and the causes of revision churn are understood and shrinking
  • Multi-state, section-level handbook editing is in customers' hands and partners can point to acknowledgment and training evidence at renewal
  • A validated, human-reviewed handoff from approved policy changes to employee distribution and payroll configuration exists, with clear ownership
  • Your scope has explicit success measures, a sequenced plan, and documented decisions on what changed and what stayed in place

How We Work

We are a new team with a clear direction and a lot still to shape. The product leaders who do well here share a few habits:

  • Precision about the problem. You know the customer, the job, and the evidence before you become attached to a solution, and you can separate what we know from what we assume.
  • Judgment, not permission-seeking. You know when to decide, when to run a test, and when a tradeoff needs a wider conversation.
  • Clear written thinking. You produce short, decision-ready documents rather than long decks.
  • Direct feedback, in both directions. You give it constructively and you ask for it.
  • Early and messy beats late and polished. A heads-up on a risk is always welcome.

Requirements & Skills

  • 5+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, with at least 3 years owning a product area end to end, from problem definition through launch, adoption, and iteration
  • A demonstrated practice of continuous customer discovery: you talk to customers and users every week, you can show the interview notes and synthesis behind your last three roadmap decisions, and you can explain which assumptions you tested and which you got wrong
  • Experience serving two or more distinct audiences for the same product (for example, a partner who buys and an employer who uses) and designing for the tension between them
  • Track record of writing product requirements and decision documents that engineering, design, and compliance experts could act on without a follow-up meeting
  • Comfort defining and defending success metrics, then changing course when the data says to
  • Experience working alongside subject-matter experts (legal, compliance, clinical, or similar) where the product has to be right, not just shipped
  • Strong collaboration with engineering, design, and data science in agile environments, including shaping AI-assisted or agentic experiences with clear human review points
  • Experience with HR technology, compliance technology, or regulatory products (preferred)
  • Experience with API-delivered, embedded, or partner-distributed products (preferred)
  • Experience with document generation, policy or content management, learning management, or workflow products where correctness and version history matter
  • Familiarity with multi-jurisdiction requirements in HR or a comparable regulated domain, or a demonstrated ability to get deep in one quickly

Education

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience

We will disclose intended pay ranges in our job ads for US-based opportunities – This role can be performed 100% remote anywhere in the US. Anticipated Pay Range: $130,000 – $160,000 Annually USD

Total compensation includes US employee benefits and annual bonus eligibility.

Benefits we offer:

  • Health, Dental & Vision Insurance *
  • 401 (k) + Employer Match *
  • Open PTO + 11 Paid Holidays + 4 Annual Paid Global Wellness Days Off
  • STD, LTD & Group Life Insurance
  • Paid Parental Leave

  • FSA & HSA Options
  • Employee Assistance Program

Perks we offer:

  • Remote Work
  • Career Advancement & Professional Development Opportunities
  • Employee Recognition

jobs.excerpt: About Nexcess Nexcess provides specialty cloud solutions for organizations where performance and compliance have to coexist.
jobs.description:
About Nexcess

Nexcess provides specialty cloud solutions for organizations where performance and compliance have to coexist. We serve businesses worldwide, from agencies scaling client sites to enterprises running mission-critical operations. We've built our reputation on deep technical expertise and genuine partnership with every client we work with. Behind every environment we manage is a team of people who take the craft seriously and keep showing up when it matters.

Overview

The Service Delivery Manager owns the customer journey from signed agreement through go-live, including new implementations and customer migrations. This role translates scope into an executable delivery plan, leads customer kickoffs, manages schedules and dependencies, coordinates cross-functional resources, and drives environments successfully into production.

This is a technical service delivery role requiring strong working knowledge of cloud and private cloud infrastructure, virtualization, networking, storage, backup, and disaster recovery. While Engineering owns technical execution, the Service Delivery Manager owns the plan, timeline, communication, coordination, and overall delivery outcome.

The Service Delivery Manager also develops and maintains the standards, processes, documentation, and project artifacts used to deliver consistent customer implementations and migrations at scale.

The compensation range for this position is between $125k-$155k.

Responsibilities

Implementation & Migration Delivery

  • Own the customer journey from signed agreement through go-live, including scope, planning, sequencing, delivery, and customer communication.
  • Lead technical implementations and migrations using structured project management practices, including kickoffs, schedules, milestone tracking, risk management, status reporting, and formal go-live sign-off.
  • Manage private cloud migration programs, including multi-wave and multi-customer migrations.
  • Coordinate dependency mapping, resource sequencing, network and IP changes, cutover planning, rollback criteria, and post-cutover validation.
  • Own and improve time-to-value for Managed Cloud implementations.
  • Identify and escalate delivery risks, dependencies, and blockers early with clear mitigation or recovery plans.
  • Maintain scope discipline and ensure changes are addressed through appropriate change-control and commercial processes.

Customer & Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as the primary delivery owner and escalation point throughout implementation and migration projects.
  • Coordinate Engineering, Solution Engineering, Support, Customer Success, Technical Account Management, Sales, and other stakeholders around a single delivery plan.
  • Partner with Sales and Solution Engineering during complex pre-sales engagements to support discovery, evaluate delivery risk, estimate effort, and validate feasibility.
  • Ensure customer expectations, contractual commitments, delivery plans, and internal execution remain aligned.
  • Lead customer kickoffs that establish scope, responsibilities, prerequisites, timelines, escalation paths, communication expectations, and definitions of completion.

Process & Delivery Standards

  • Build and maintain the Managed Cloud implementation playbook, including kickoff templates, onboarding plans, runbooks, welcome materials, and standard project artifacts.
  • Develop, document, version, and maintain SOPs for implementation and migration processes.
  • Partner with technical and customer-facing teams to ensure processes are practical, scalable, and aligned with actual delivery capabilities.
  • Develop documentation appropriate for different audiences, including technical runbooks, internal enablement materials, and customer-facing onboarding resources.
  • Drive adoption of established processes through training, reinforcement, measurement, and review.
  • Facilitate post-mortems and incorporate customer and internal feedback into continuous process improvement.
  • Identify opportunities for automation and partner with Engineering and Product to reduce unnecessary manual effort.

Program & Team Leadership

  • Maintain program schedules across multiple customers, migration waves, dependencies, resources, and critical-path activities.
  • Report implementation status, capacity, risks, and delivery performance to Managed Cloud leadership.
  • Establish scalable project management practices as implementation volume grows.
  • Hire, develop, and lead project managers and migration coordinators as the function expands.
  • Travel approximately 5–10% as business needs require.

Additional Expectations

  • Demonstrates and promotes the company's Impact Behaviors in all interactions and decision-making.
    • Design
    • Ownership
    • First Team
    • Performance
  • Maintains a professional, collaborative, and client-focused approach while supporting team and organizational objectives.
  • Performs other duties, responsibilities, and special projects as assigned to meet business needs.

Qualifications

Required

  • B2B customers, including at least 2 years supporting mid-market or enterprise engagements.
  • Strong working knowledge of cloud and private cloud infrastructure, virtualization, compute, storage, networking, backup, and disaster recovery.
  • Experience delivering cloud or infrastructure migrations involving platforms such as AWS, Azure, GCP, VMware, Nutanix, Hyper-V, or managed hosting environments.
  • Experience managing migration activities including discovery, dependency mapping, wave planning, cutover planning, IP and DNS changes, rollback criteria, and post-cutover validation.
  • Experience supporting projects from pre-sales discovery and scoping through implementation and production delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain complex project schedules involving dependencies, resource sequencing, milestones, and critical-path activities.
  • Experience developing and implementing delivery processes, SOPs, runbooks, and repeatable project standards.
  • Strong technical writing skills with the ability to produce clear and actionable documentation.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and coordinate cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority.
  • Experience with Agile delivery practices, including backlogs, prioritization, stand-ups, acceptance criteria, and iterative delivery.
  • Strong project management fundamentals, including work breakdown, dependency management, risk tracking, change control, and executive-level reporting.
  • Direct customer-facing delivery experience with mid-market or enterprise stakeholders.
  • Experience using project management or PSA tools such as Linear, Jira, Smartsheet, Asana, Monday, Kantata, or similar platforms.
  • Ability to independently manage complex projects, identify risks, escalate concerns, and drive work through completion.

Preferred

  • Experience within managed hosting, managed cloud, private cloud, or MSP environments.
  • Experience managing repeatable, multi-wave migration programs.
  • Agile delivery certification such as CSM, PSM, or SAFe; demonstrated experience is valued over certification.
  • Experience applying Scrum or Kanban methodologies within customer delivery environments.
  • Experience defining and implementing self-service and human-led delivery models.
  • Experience building or scaling a project management or service delivery team.
  • Experience supporting Nutanix migration programs.

Key Performance Indicators

  • Maintain customer onboarding satisfaction of 90% or higher, with feedback collected and addressed following completed implementations.
  • Achieve on-time delivery of 90% or higher against customer commitments established during project kickoff.
  • Improve average time-to-value from signed agreement through go-live by 30% within 12 months.
  • Deliver migration programs according to approved schedules without unplanned customer-impacting downtime attributable to planning or coordination.
  • Establish and maintain standardized implementation processes and project artifacts across new Managed Cloud implementations.
  • Maintain documented scope baselines and change logs for active projects.
  • Improve early customer retention and satisfaction through consistent implementation quality.
  • Increase the number of successfully implemented customers willing to serve as customer references.

Work Environment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an individual to successfully perform the essential duties of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties.

  • While performing the essential duties of this job, the individual is regularly required to speak and hear
  • While performing the essential duties of this job, the individual is regularly required to use hands for keyboarding, gross manipulation, and fine manipulation
  • Works at a desk and computer screen for extended periods of time
  • Works in a traditional climate controlled office environment or from home
  • Works in a highly stressful environment dealing with a wide variety of challenges, deadlines and diverse employee population

Disclaimer

Additional duties and tasks may be assigned as part of the job function. jobs.description:
Lead Specialist, Technical Architect (Quality) - ExamDeveloper

About ExamDeveloper

ExamDeveloper is a web-based exam development platform that allows customers to write, review, and manage questions on their exams. Customers rely on ExamDeveloper to support the full workflow around item writing, collaborative review, scoring, and test management.

ExamDeveloper is feature-rich and used by clients in a variety of ways, which creates a high volume of testing, automation, and release-readiness decisions. The product is supported by multiple Agile software development teams and a large distributed quality engineering community, including many QA engineers based in India. Clear asynchronous communication and consistent quality standards are essential to the role.

As a Quality Engineer Architect aligned to the E30 expert track, you provide domain-level quality leadership for ExamDeveloper. This role is unique within the ExamDeveloper quality organization and is not intended to define a standard Lead progression step. This is not a people manager role, but it does provide technical direction, standards, coaching, artifact review, and quality-process leadership across multiple Agile teams and a large distributed QA organization.

You are the subject-matter expert on the domain, on automation approaches, and on the scenarios that matter most to customers — and you think like an end customer of the product. You are relied upon when quality challenges are highly complex, ambiguous, cross-system, or business-critical, and when decisions require strong judgment across test strategy, automation architecture, reliability, and release confidence. You lead through expertise, not formal authority — shaping the quality system, mentoring senior engineers, reviewing critical QA work, and spending selective hands-on time in testing or automation investigation where your expertise has the greatest impact.

Key responsibilities

Quality strategy and direction

  • Set strategic direction for the ExamDeveloper quality system, including process, automation, tooling, training, metrics, quality gates, and release confidence across the domain.

  • Partner with the Product Architect and Engineering leadership to determine long-term automation and quality strategy.

  • Continually evaluate the process, tools, technology, data, and people practices involved in QA work, then drive improvements that make testing more automated, efficient, sustainable, and aligned to business risk.

  • Establish quality metrics that inform decision-making, including automation health, test reliability, defect leakage, cycle time, release readiness, and the effectiveness of QA investments.

Subject-matter expertise

  • Serve as the domain subject-matter expert on quality, automation approaches, and critical test scenarios.

jobs.excerpt: Posit's mission is to create free and open-source software for data science, scientific research, and technical communication to enhance the production and consumption of knowledge by everyone, regardless of economic means.
jobs.description:
Posit's mission is to create free and open-source software for data science, scientific research, and technical communication to enhance the production and consumption of knowledge by everyone, regardless of economic means. We are a different kind of software company, and we’re proud to build and sell products that help people understand and improve the world through data.

About the Team

Posit’s Solutions Engineering (Sol-Eng) team aims to reduce the distance between customers of our professional products and open source offerings.

We help our customers – especially their IT/SysAdmin teams – deploy, install, configure, and use our professional products. We aim to bring curiosity and empathy to every customer engagement, leaning into the customer experiences as they seek to get value from open source data science.

But that’s only half the job.

As we learn about what customers want and need, we use that knowledge to improve our products, documentation, and processes.

On Sol-Eng, you’ll play an essential role in both unblocking and empowering customers and making Posit and our products work better in the future.

People who thrive in this role tend to:

  • Find joy in working directly with and unblocking customers. This role is customer-facing.
  • Love learning and sharing your knowledge of the server infrastructure and architecture that underlies enterprise data science. You’ll be an advisor to IT teams who administer Posit’s products in a wide variety of architectures and with a range of integrations. You have exposure to some of these topics and technologies (e.g. cloud services, Linux, Kubernetes, Docker, Slurm, authentication, connecting to data sources) and look forward to opportunities to dive deeply and learn in other areas. Knowing all of these topics on Day 1 is not required, but having interest in learning more about how they work is fundamental to the job.
  • Be curious about data science workflows and use cases.We make tools to multiply the impact of Data Scientists who work in open source. You won’t be doing data science or writing code, but you’ll need to understand what a Data Scientist does (e.g., exploratory data analysis, modeling, reporting, app development). . Prior experience specifically with data science or our professional products is not necessary, but may be helpful.
  • Be hungry and humble. Sol-Eng covers an impossibly broad technical scope.. Great Sol-Eng team members are quick to admit what they don’t know and constantly seek to learn more. As a trusted advisor to customers, your credibility comes from being honest about the limits of your knowledge and following through to close the gaps.
  • Find excitement in having many demands on your time, rather than overwhelm. The Sol-Eng team has close relationships with almost every other team at Posit. There’s no limit to the different projects Sol-Eng could take on, being able to choose important things (with help and guidance from managers) and ignore distractions is a key skill for a Posit Solutions Engineer.

What you’ll own own:

  • Serving as a proactive, ongoing technical advisor to customers discussing server configurations and architectures, supporting technical strategy planning, and sharing best practices for doing open source data science at scale with Posit’s professional products. You’ll collaborate with sales and customer success to enable the customer to realize the full value of their Posit environment.
  • Scaling our reach through webinars, talks, workshops, documentation, automation, and how-tos that help customers adopt Posit products.
  • Leading scoped, project-based implementation work, from onboarding through delivery of defined outcomes.
  • Providing the voice of the customer to other teams at Posit, especially Product Management and Product Engineering.

What you’ll help with:

  • Improving our team’s processes so our workflows facilitate us doing great work, taking adequate focus time, and having time off to rest and recharge.
  • Setting the direction of our products by influencing the Product Management and engineering teams.

You will learn...

So much.

No one has ever (or ever will) start on Sol-Eng knowing everything we do. Strong candidates for this role generally have prior experience with approximately half of the things below.

  • How to navigate deeply technical post-sales customer calls and have the ability to speak about technical topics to internal and external audiences of different levels. Even people with substantial customer experience find that Sol-Eng demands new depths of empathy, curiosity, and clarity of thinking and explanation.
  • How Posit’s Pro Products work. On customer calls, you will be the expert on our Pro Products – explaining how to install and configure them, as well as how they help make life better for Data Scientists.
  • How to speak fluently about enterprise infrastructure. Solutions Engineers help our customers IT/Admins determine the best product architecture for them, which requires they speak knowledgeably about integrations to other data (science) tools and platforms, and how to get things done on Linux servers including system administration, authentication, networking, and virtualization.

What to expect:

Within 1 month, you’ll…

  • Meet the rest of the Sol-Eng team and start meeting members of Customer Success, Sales, and other nearby teams.
  • Configure Posit’s Pro Products for yourself to start learning the ins and outs.
  • Have joined dozens of IT architecture and post-sales calls with IT/Admins of Posit’s Pro products.

Within 3 months, you’ll...

  • Lead customer calls, helping our customers determine how Posit’s Pro products fit into their existing data and technology stacks. You won’t need to know all the answers, but you will lead with curiosity to build the right mental models that will allow you to go back to find answers.
  • Be comfortable discussing general architectures and deployment patterns for our product
  • Begin getting hands on with customers who are installing and maintaining our products, looking over their shoulders and suggesting how to set up and configure their environments.

Within 12 months, you’ll…

  • Contribute to projects in roles of escalating size and scope.
  • Take on larger, more strategic, and higher-touch customer engagements that might include weekly meetings with the same customer.

Posit offers competitive compensation with extensive human-first, people-focused benefits to prioritize your personal and financial well-being. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, and skillset. This hiring range reflects base salary and assumes that the job will be performed in the United States.

Hiring Range
$141,800—$187,110 USD

Working at Posit:

  • We welcome all talented colleagues and are committed to a culture that represents diversity in all its forms.
  • We prioritize giving ourselves “focus time” to get deep work done. We minimize meetings and attempt to operate asynchronously.
  • We are a learning organization and take mentorship and career growth seriously. We hope to learn from you and we anticipate that you will also deepen your skills, influence, and leadership as a result of working at Posit.
  • We operate under a unique sustainable business model: We have over 50% of our engineering dedicated to creating free and open source software. We are profitable and we plan to be around decades from now.
  • Posit is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) and a Certified B Corporation®, which means our open-source mission is codified into our charter. As a result, our corporate decisions balance the community's interests, customers, employees, and shareholders. Hear more about why we think this matters here.

Notable:

We offer competitive compensation with extensive human-first, people-focused benefits to prioritize your personal and financial well-being. These benefits apply to full-time positions only.

  • 100% of medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums are covered for employees and their families! Fertility and gender-affirming healthcare is included in all of our plans.
  • Supplemental mental health and wellness benefits are available via Ginger even if you don’t opt in to our insurance plans, including Ginger for teen family members.
  • Posit's gender-neutral paid parental leave policy covers all new parents, including foster and adoptive parents.
  • All full-time employees are eligible for 401k enrollment starting on day one.
    • After six months of employment, Posit provides a substantial yearly match to employee 401K contributions.
  • An annual profit-sharing bonus for employees recognizes our team’s contributions to company performance across the year.
  • We are a 100% distributed team. You are also welcome to come into our Boston office.
    • We offer a $400 monthly reimbursement for coworking space rental if you prefer to work away from home.
  • Our Lifestyle Savings Account offers an initial deposit of $1800 and then an additional quarterly stipend of $375 to cover the costs of professional development, wellness, financial health, charitable giving, and remote work support.
  • We provide a flexible environment with a generous vacation policy that encourages a minimum of four weeks PTO per year plus 15 paid company holidays.

Are you excited about this role but not sure if your experience aligns with every qualification in the job description? That’s okay. We know multiple perspectives are essential for a thriving organization and we'd still love to hear from you!

An Infrastructure Solutions Engineer makes Planet's infrastructure easier to use. Infra Solutions is a small, multi-disciplinary team: engineers who are as comfortable operating a system as building one, and as comfortable in a hard conversation as in a code review. We sit between the teams who build Planet's platform capabilities and the teams who need them, and our market is every engineering team at Planet, which we earn one engagement at a time. This role carries the day to day of that. A senior engineer works alongside you on the parts that are still ambiguous, so you are not expected to walk into a fogged problem alone. You will spend a lot of your time in other teams' repositories, channels and problems. This is a role driven by unreasonable hospitality (value out of proportion to what anyone asked us for) and built on solid engineering and operational fundamentals.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. If located near a Planet office, you are expected to work from that office 3 days per week.

Who We Are & What We Do:

Branching Minds’ mission is to empower all educators to effectively, efficiently, and equitably support the holistic needs of their students; and to create a path to academic and personal success for every learner. Already supporting over 2,000,000 students across 400+ districts from over 40 states, our vision is to be the most effective national K12 school district solution for achieving high-fidelity MTSS/RTI; consistently demonstrating our ability to save teachers' planning/documenting time, improve outcomes of our students, and eliminate achievement gaps.

Branching Minds is also a Benefit Corporation. We prioritize mission alongside profit. We embrace self-management, transparency, collaboration, initiative, and making a difference in the world.

If using innovation to reimagine education in service of equity energizes you -- join our team!

The Calling:

Engaging the full scope of your skills, passion, and creativity in sales, you’ll get to build partnerships with district leaders and help them achieve student success for all learners.

We’re looking for an Account Executive who can succeed across the full sales cycle, from the first outbound touch to signed contract, and who takes ownership of building and advancing a healthy pipeline. You'll own new business with large K-12 districts in your territory and spend meaningful time in the field with prospects and customers.

Selling to school districts requires more than a great product. It takes curiosity, persistence, and the ability to understand complex challenges, connect our solutions to district priorities, and build a compelling case for investment. You’ll navigate multiple stakeholders, manage complex buying processes, and bring the strategic thinking and sales discipline needed to move opportunities forward and close business.

As part of the Revenue team, this role reports to the Director of Sales.

What You Will Achieve:

Keeping your pipeline full

  • Proactively identify and pursue new client relationships with large districts (10,000+ students in size) in your sales territory.
  • Book 1-2 new meetings of your own every week, whether through engagement in the field, email and phone outreach, or other creative approaches. You’ll also receive meetings from inbound leads and our Sales Development Representative, but you won’t succeed in this role without booking your own.

  • Start and finish your prospecting sequences and campaigns. No random acts of prospecting!
  • Consistently bring new ideas to your 1:1s with your manager: campaigns, sequences, territory trips, and conference ideas.

Winning complex, multi-stakeholder deals

  • Ask excellent discovery questions to understand prospect needs, challenges, and goals, and tie Branching Minds’ products and features directly to school and district pain points.
  • Strategically map accounts and engage with key decision-makers across multiple stakeholders.
  • Prepare thoroughly for every meeting and follow up promptly afterward.
  • Leave nothing to chance: set a scheduled next step on every deal, and work your pipeline in between scheduled meetings.
  • Develop accurate proposals and contracts that reflect both the client’s needs and the capability of Branching Minds, and negotiate and close with skill.
  • Consistently meet or exceed quarterly sales quotas, pipeline growth, and activity metrics.

Building relationships with district leaders

  • Spend ample time in the field with prospects and customers alike.
  • Represent Branching Minds at industry conferences and networking events to expand market presence and deepen industry knowledge.
  • Earn referrals. You’ll know you’re an expert relationship-builder when the district leaders you’ve sold to or spent time with refer you to their peers.
  • Work closely with Implementation and Customer Success teams to ensure a smooth transition post-sale, high client satisfaction, and long-term partnerships within your accounts.

Executing with operational excellence

  • Manage your pipeline and performance independently, with a data-driven approach that uses key metrics to guide decisions.
  • Maintain comprehensive and up-to-date records of all customer interactions in HubSpot, including deal stages, close dates, qualification information, timelines, and next steps.
  • Quickly learn our product, our space, and the problems our buyers need to solve, and stay informed of industry trends and the competitive landscape.
  • Work independently, but never be afraid to ask for help if it increases the chances you win a deal.
  • Contribute to the refinement of sales processes, tools, and methodologies, and support the growth and development of other Account Executives on the Large Market team.

Requirements

Why We Want You:

  • 5+ years of K-12 ed-tech sales experience selling to public school districts.
  • You have prior experience as an SDR/BDR and succeeded. You know the power of prospecting and never feel above the work that made you successful.
  • A track record of moving up through the ranks (for example, SDR to SMB to large market) at a reputable K12, ed-tech company.
  • You bring a proven record of meeting or exceeding quota and closing deals with districts of 10,000+ students.
  • Demonstrated success in an outbound motion. You can describe in detail a specific campaign or approach that led to booked discovery meetings.
  • Experience engaging with senior district decision-makers, with a strong ability to build rapport and trust.
  • Strong organizational systems that let you consistently finish the sequences and campaigns you start, prepare well for every meeting, follow up on time, and manage your pipeline with limited supervision.
  • Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to present complex solutions effectively.
  • Experience using HubSpot or an equivalent CRM, and a commitment to keeping it accurate.
  • Comfortable traveling at least 40% to meet with prospects and customers and attend industry events (especially during higher-volume times of year like fall and spring).

Lucky Us If You:

(No biggie if you don’t)

Interview Process:

If we are a match, you can expect a total of 3 steps in the interview process after the initial application

  • 30-minute initial conversation with the Director of Sales
  • 45-minute panel discussion with a member of Sales Team Leadership & a peer Account Executive
  • 30-minute final conversation with the Director of Sales

Benefits

What We Offer You:

  • Check out our Benefits & Perks
  • Fully remote!
  • An awesome, cross-disciplinary, mission-driven team solving meaningful problems that improves the lives of educators and students.

Reporting to the Associate Director, Sales Operations Reporting & Analytics, the Manager of Sales Operations will provide integrated Incentive Compensation (IC), sales reporting, and sales analytics support for assigned field teams. The role will translate commercial data into actionable insights, support accurate and compliant IC administration, and partner with Sales Leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to improve field execution, decision-making, and operational scalability.

This role will own recurring and ad hoc analytics, contribute to IC plan design, administration, and governance, and help build and strengthen the processes, documentation, controls, analytical capabilities, and technical requirements needed to support a scalable and sustainable IC operating model. Incentive Compensation Administration, Analytics & Governance

  • Support end-to-end execution of semester IC plans, including timelines, field sales roster and eligibility inputs, sales quota methodology, account allocations, individual performance objectives, kickers, contests, payout calculations, IC statements, and field communications.
  • Develop, validate, and explain IC reporting, attainment results, payout calculations, variance drivers, and exceptions for Sales Leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Perform quality control of IC data, calculations, outputs, and vendor deliverables; document issues, root causes, decisions, corrective actions, and approvals in an audit-ready manner.
  • Maintain IC business rules, plan guides, process documentation, decision logs, exception logs, version control, and supporting materials to strengthen consistency, transparency, and compliance.
  • Partner on IC plan modeling, scenario analysis, goal setting, payout curves, budget impact, fairness, and plan effectiveness.
  • Partner with and support first-line managers and their teams to achieve operational excellence.
  • Train new hires and provide ongoing education on Sales Operations topics.
  • Collaborate effectively across all Braeburn cross-functional teams.

Sales Reporting, Analytics & Insights

  • Ensure accurate and timely delivery of Field Reports in collaboration with technical data teams.
  • Create and enhance standard and ad hoc reports and analyses leveraging field engagement activity, Braeburn trade sales data, secondary data, CRM data, and other approved sources to support sales force effectiveness.
  • Deliver team-specific territory, account, targeting, execution, and performance insights that explain what is happening, why it matters, and recommended next actions.
  • Monitor report accuracy and consistency; reconcile source data, document assumptions, identify root causes, and coordinate issue resolution with internal and external partners.
  • Support recurring leadership reporting, dashboards, performance reviews, monthly territory summaries, and executive-ready insights with clear narratives and documented methodologies.
  • Identify opportunities to standardize, automate, and scale recurring analyses while strengthening data governance and reducing manual effort and rework.

  • Serve as a primary Sales Operations partner for assigned field teams, providing integrated support across IC, reporting, analytics, targeting, and related business rules.
  • Partner with Sales Leadership, Finance, Human Resources, Compliance, Legal, Business Operations, Data Operations, Sales Planning, Training, and technology partners to align assumptions, timelines, decisions, and communications.
  • Support account-based targeting, territory and account performance analysis, allocations, roster changes, and downstream reporting or IC impacts in collaboration with responsible functional owners.
  • Train field sales employees and provide ongoing education on IC, reporting, data interpretation, inquiry processes, and applicable Sales Operations tools.
  • Contribute to Sales Operations initiatives and maintain clear project plans, owners, milestones, risks, decisions, and follow-up actions.

Required Skills:

  • Advanced analytical skills, with strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Working knowledge of CRM tools, business intelligence, data warehouse, and reporting environments.

Important Notice for Applicants:
